articles.content_orig:
Gable Steveson had a lot to say in his first statement after suffering a devastating knockout loss at UFC 331 this past weekend, but instead of focusing on the loss, it seems he mostly wanted to address sexual assault allegations from his past while he was competing at the University of Minnesota.
Gable Steveson responds to sexual assault allegations in first statement since knockout loss at UFC 331
Gable Steveson broke his silence on Tuesday with his first statement after UFC 331
On Tuesday, Steveson released a prepared statement discussing his 12-second knockout loss at UFC 331, focused primarily on responding to opponent Sean Sharaf repeatedly calling him a “rapist” in the days leading up to their fight.
In 2019, Steveson was arrested on sexual misconduct charges. He has always maintained his innocence in the case, and the charges were eventually dropped due to “inadequate evidence.” Steveson was released without facing any criminal penalty. Now seven years later, those allegations came to light again after Sharaf repeatedly called Steveson “a rapist” and “loophole” in the leadup to their fight, and the 2020 Olympic gold medalist decided to address the situation as well as his first-ever loss in the UFC.
Read the full statement below:
“This statement is for my family, my friends, my fans and the people who truly know me and know the kind of man I am. I know there are people who will never support me, no matter what I say or do. That’s their choice. But I’m speaking to the people who know me not just as an athlete but as a husband and a father to a young daughter. Prior to and during fight week, an incident from my college years was brought up by my opponent. I believe it was raised to get in my head but it also reopened something that had been addressed years ago. I want to be clear — I did not do anything alleged. I was never charged with a crime and he matter was ultimately dropped by the district attorney. The allegations were not ignored nor brushed aside. They were thoroughly and heavily reviewed as I fully cooperated with law enforcement, including a seprate Title IX review.
“There were no criminal charges, no conviction, and no finding of responsibility against me. The matter was closed and there is no pending legal issue involving me. My own attorney did their own investigation and stated on the record that even if the law was changed, I would have the same outcome, which now speaks for itself.
I understand how serious allegations like this are and I understand that people may hve questions qhen they hear only part of a story. Moving forward, I am going to keep focusing on my wife, my daughter, my family and he work in front of me. To the people who support me, thank you. I know who I am. My family knows who I am. The people who have walked with me through live know who I am. That’s what maters to me and that’s where I’m going to keep my focus.
“As for my opponent, congratulations, you caught me. A mistake on my end was made. It was your night. Just like my wrestling days after my loss, I came bacbk with an undeniable will to win and focus that led me to the top of my sport. The result of Saturday night, I believe, will catapult me to do the same. I will be great and this won’t deny me.”
Steveson has been called the greatest prospect to enter the sport of MMA thanks to his long list of accolades in wrestling, which includes his Olympic gold medal-winning performance at the 2020 games.
Following his knockout loss this past Saturday, Steveson left the octagon in a hurry without offering Sharaf congratulations on his win, although former UFC two-division champion Jon Jones took responsibility for that decision because he wanted his protégé to get immediate medical attention.

articles.title_orig: "You shouldn't be here": Trump calls out CNN's Kaitlan Collins at U.N.
articles.title_zh: "You shouldn't be here": Trump calls out CNN's Kaitlan Collins at U.N.
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump lashed out at a CNN journalist Tuesday morning at the United Nations, telling her, "You should not be here covering me," as the Department of Justice prepares to defend in federal court his ban on that media outlet, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.
CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins had asked Trump about a new poll that found two-thirds of Americans do not think the U.S. is winning its war with Iran.
"When will it end?" Collins asked the president.
"So it's an honor to be here. I'm surprised that CNN is here covering me," Trump told reporters as he gestured at Collins, before he entered the General Assembly in New York to address that body.
Collins interjected, "The United Nations allowed us in here, sir."
"You should not be here," Trump told Collins. "You should not be here covering me. You said you weren't going to cover me."
After Trump left, Collins later noted on air, "We never said we were never going to cover the president."
"We will continue to cover the president despite their efforts to block CNN from the White House grounds," she said.
Trump last Friday said he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, citing what he called false stories about him and his administration. Trump has frequently criticized news coverage of him and did not point to specific stories.
That ban took effect Saturday morning, when Secret Service officers at the White House took press passes from journalists from those three outlets when they arrived to work there.
On Monday, the three outlets filed a lawsuit against Trump in U.S. District Court in Washington, asking a judge to block the president's ban and restore their access to the White House. The suit alleges Trump violated the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution and the Constitution's Due Process Clause in summarily barring the outlets.
"We are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the outlets said in a joint statement on Monday.
Also Monday, the five-member consortium of TV news networks that rotates pool coverage of the White House said four of those networks would suspend pool coverage ahead of Trump's trip to New York because the White House was not allowing CNN to act as the pool as was originally scheduled. It's not clear if that suspension will continue when Trump returns to Washington and another outlet is scheduled to act as the White House TV pool.
The consortium, which includes ABC News, CBS News, Fox News and NBC News, in addition to CNN, provides video of Trump events to other media outlets for their use.
The suspension of pool coverage does not change how CNN or the other networks separately cover Trump's visit to New York and the UN.
Kelly, the Trump-appointed judge assigned to handle the lawsuit challenging his media ban, has ordered the Department of Justice to respond to the outlets' request for an injunction against the ban on Tuesday.
Kelly scheduled a teleconference hearing on the request for Wednesday.
Trump told reporters on Tuesday that he expected Kelly to rule against him and asked whether he would let the outlets back into the White House if the judge ordered it.
"It probably will, because this is a judge who's not a particularly fair judge," Trump said of Kelly.
In November 2018, Kelly ordered the White House to restore the press pass of then-CNN correspondent Jim Acosta, whose credentials had been revoked after a contentious exchange with Trump.
MS NOW reported Tuesday that it had obtained talking points the White House had sent congressional Republicans about Trump's ban of the outlets. Talking points are designed to be used as a response to questions from journalists about a specific topic.
Among other things, the talking points say, "No president has been more transparent or offered more of his time to the press," and, "the First Amendment protects their right to publish; it does not entitle certain outlets and members of the press to a hard pass, briefing room seat, or place in the press pool." A "hard pass" is a long-term press credential for journalists who regularly cover the White House.
"Fabricating facts or reporting verifiable falsehoods from inside the White House complex is an intentional breach of professional decorum and it is severely disruptive to the mission and purpose of the White House," another talking point says.
Disclosure: CNBC and MS NOW are divisions of Versant Media.

articles.title_orig: Resetting expectations for these six NFL teams with injured quarterbacks: Giants eyeing draft again
articles.title_zh: 重新设定对这六支四分卫受伤的NFL球队的期望：巨人队再次关注选秀
articles.summary_zh: 到目前为止，四分卫受伤一直是2026年NFL赛季的不幸故事。在第二周的训练营中，六名先发球员的缺席使联盟近四分之一的场上比赛黯然失色。幸运的是，许多伤病都是短期问题，只有轻微的破坏竞选的风险，但在少数情况下，几乎没有理由乐观。
articles.content_orig:
Quarterback injuries have been the unfortunate story of the 2026 NFL season thus far. The loss of six starters from training camp through Week 2 overshadows on-field play for nearly one quarter of the league. Fortunately, many of the injuries are short-term issues with only a slight risk of derailing the campaign, but in a couple of cases, there is little reason for optimism.
The New York Giants might be in the worst position of any of the six teams that lost their starters. Jaxson Dart sustained a knee injury on "Monday Night Football" that, upon further testing, is more severe than the team initially feared. If any of the NFL's injured signal-callers are to miss the rest of the year, Dart is the most likely candidate.
If it is indeed a season-ender for Dart, the Giants' 2026 goals shift dramatically. For other teams, like the Seattle Seahawks, expectations remain largely unchanged even in the face of injury.
Here are reasonable expectations for all six teams with injured quarterbacks.
Injured player: Jaxson Dart (knee)
New expectations: Vie for another early draft pick
There is no sugar coating the Giants' outlook without Dart. What had all the makings of a (finally) exciting year is already down the tubes. The offense looked hapless with Jameis Winston on in relief against the Los Angeles Rams, and while the veteran has had decent stretches in the past, his diminished arm strength, persistent turnover problems and the immense downgrade in mobility he brings compared to Dart puts a firm ceiling on the Giants.
Winston will potentially man the offense for the remainder of the year after Dart's MRI revealed a worse injury than expected. In five games without Dart since his arrival as a first-round pick, the Giants are 0-5. That history suggests that so long as Winston is the man under center, New York will stand among the worst teams in the NFL. The silver lining is that the Giants should be able to add more premium young talent to their enticing core in the 2027 draft, but this was supposed to be a season in which that group elevated them out of the early draft pick range and into playoff contention.
Injured players: Caleb Williams (hamstring), Tyson Bagent (concussion)
New expectations: Fall into early-season hole, climb out when Williams returns
The hamstring issue that knocked Williams out of the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings initially looked like it would result in a long-term absence. Instead, the rising star is week-to-week and could even return as soon as Monday's battle with the Philadelphia Eagles. It would be aggressive to bring him back from a soft-tissue injury in such short order, though, and with Bagent suffering a concussion, there is a real chance the Bears roll out their No. 3 quarterback on "Monday Night Football." Case Keenum might make his first appearance since 2023.
If it ends up being no more than a one-game absence for Williams, the Bears will likely be 1-2 upon his return. The early-season losses might hold Chicago back from reaching its loftiest regular-season goals, but by no means would they dash the Bears' hopes of reaching the playoffs. The offense is electric enough with Williams in the lineup to rattle off a bunch of victories. Remember, this team started 0-2 a year ago and reached the divisional round of the playoffs.
Injured player: Jayden Daniels (dislocated elbow)
New expectations: Another losing season incoming
With two losses already on their ledger, the Commanders are in extreme danger of falling back into the NFL's bottom tier for a second consecutive season. It is difficult to foresee them stringing together wins with Daniels on the sideline, particularly because their next six games include matchups against the NFC West's top three teams and a rematch with the Eagles squad that defeated them in Week 1. Washington might have to attack that entire stretch with Marcus Mariota under center.
The dislocated elbow is the exact same injury Daniels sustained in Week 9 last year. He missed four weeks and reinjured the elbow in his return and sat out the remainder of the season. The recurring nature of this issue sounds alarms about Daniels' ability to stay on the field this year and beyond. And the rest of the team is not strong enough to stay afloat without him. The defense, for instance, ranks 27th in scoring through two games.
Injured player: Sam Darnold (glute)
New expectations: Contend for second consecutive Super Bowl
Drew Lock did just enough to lead the Seahawks to a season-opening win when thrust into action in the first quarter, and following a full week of preparation for the road opener at the Arizona Cardinals, he excelled with three touchdowns in a 31-7 win. Seattle should be in business for as long as it needs to roll out its backup.
Even better news for the Seahawks is that Sam Darnold might return to action this week. Coach Mike Macdonald said he anticipates Darnold suiting up for practice, and the extent of his participation will determine his availability for Sunday's matchup against the Commanders. Assuming the offense is back at full strength no later than Week 4, the Seahawks have a good chance of remaining undefeated in time for Darnold's return. They cannot ask for much more than that.
Injured player: Kyler Murray (concussion)
New expectations: Battle for NFC North title
The concussion Murray suffered in the first quarter of the season opener looked grim, but it will result in only a one-game absence. Murray cleared concussion protocol and will start in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, coach Kevin O'Connell announced. Thanks to Carson Wentz and two solid performances, Murray inherits a 2-0 record for his return.
In a division where every other team is 1-1 and where the Bears have quarterback injuries, the Packers look flawed, and the Lions' defense is a mess, Minnesota has a chance to build a comfortable early-season cushion. None of the teams on their schedule until Week 9 made the playoffs in 2025. If Murray delivers the career resurgence the Vikings hoped he would when they signed him in free agency, he could lead them to a terrific first half of the season.
Injured player: Michael Penix Jr. (torn ACL), Tua Tagovailoa (oblique)
New expectations: Prevent disastrous season after 0-2 start
The Cooper Rush experience was dismal. Back-to-back losses and a 34-3 drubbing at the hands of a division rival made the Falcons look like one of the NFL's worst teams through two weeks. Help is on the way, though. Penix is cleared for action and will take over as the starter in Week 3, and Tagovailoa returned to full participation in practice, setting him up to assume backup duties. Health willing, Atlanta will not need to turn back to its No. 3 quarterback.
The problem is that Penix is not guaranteed to be an upgrade. He is 4-8 as a starter since his arrival in 2024 and has an immense injury history. He ought to be able to make better use of his elite offensive supporting cast than Rush, but it would require a breakout season from the third-year pro in order for the Falcons to erase their 0-2 start and finish the year above .500. And if things go sideways for Penix or he returns to the injury report, Tagovailoa carries the exact same shortcomings.
articles.content_zh:
到目前为止，四分卫受伤一直是2026年NFL赛季的不幸故事。在第二周的训练营中，六名先发球员的缺席使联盟近四分之一的场上比赛黯然失色。幸运的是，许多伤病都是短期问题，只有轻微的破坏竞选的风险，但在少数情况下，几乎没有理由乐观。
纽约巨人队可能是六支失去首发球员的球队中最糟糕的一支。Jaxson Dart在“周一晚上足球”中膝盖受伤，经过进一步测试，伤势比球队最初担心的更严重。如果NFL的任何受伤的信号呼叫者错过了今年剩下的时间，Dart是最有可能的候选人。
如果这确实是达特的赛季结束，那么巨人队2026年的进球将发生巨大变化。对于其他球队，如西雅图海鹰队，即使面对伤病，人们的期望也基本保持不变。
以下是对所有六支四分卫受伤的球队的合理预期。
受伤球员：Jaxson Dart（膝盖）
新的期望：期待另一个早期选秀权
没有达特，巨人队的前景就没有糖衣了。（终于）激动人心的一年的所有要素都已经尘埃落定。在面对洛杉矶公羊队的比赛中，Jameis Winston替补上场，进攻看起来很倒霉，虽然这位老将过去有过不错的伸展，但他手臂力量的减弱、持续的失误问题以及与Dart相比他带来的机动性的大幅下降给巨人队带来了严峻的挑战。
在达特的核磁共振成像显示伤势比预期更严重后，温斯顿可能会在今年剩下的时间里担任进攻球员。自从达特作为首轮选秀权加盟以来，在没有达特的五场比赛中，巨人队以0比5获胜。这段历史表明，只要温斯顿是中锋，纽约将成为美国国家橄榄球联盟中最糟糕的球队之一。一线希望是，巨人队应该能够在2027年的选秀中为他们诱人的核心增加更多优秀的年轻人才，但这应该是一个该小组将他们从早期选秀范围提升到季后赛争夺的赛季。
受伤球员：Caleb Williams（腿筋），Tyson Bagent（脑震荡）
新的期望：陷入赛季初的洞，当威廉姆斯回归时爬出来
在第二周输给明尼苏达维京人队的比赛中，威廉姆斯被腿筋问题淘汰出局，最初看起来这将导致他长期缺席。相反，这颗冉冉升起的新星每周都在升起，甚至可能重新升起

articles.title_orig: Qantas’s New York-to-Sydney ‘Project Sunrise’ Flights to Take Off in 2028
articles.title_zh: 澳航纽约至悉尼的“日出计划”航班将于2028年起飞
articles.summary_zh: 纽约（WABC）-从2028年开始，航空旅客将首次获得此类航班服务……但要为长途旅行做好准备。澳航周二宣布，作为“日出计划”的一部分，澳航将于2028年年中开始开通悉尼和纽约市之间的直达航班，使其成为澳大利亚和大苹果之间有史以来第一条直达商业服务。这架18小时的航班将使往返澳大利亚的行程缩短3小时。
articles.content_orig:
Qantas says travellers will be able to fly between Sydney and New York in just 18 hours from mid-2028 when the airline launches its second ultra long-haul route, cutting at least three hours from the travel time.
The route will be the second in Qantas’ Project Sunrise expansion plans, with new Sydney to London direct flights planned for October 2027, after some delays.
It would be the first commercial direct flight from Kingsford-Smith airport to New York’s JFK airport. Qantas currently offers flights from Sydney to New York with a stopover in Los Angeles, which take 21 hours and typically cost more than $1,400 one way or more than $1,900 return.
Qantas has not disclosed prices for the Project Sunrise routes. It has previously suggested direct fares could cost 20% more than stopover fares and said ticket prices are facing upward pressure.
Tickets for the Sydney to New York route are set to go on sale in August 2027, Qantas said. It has not specified which month flights will begin. When it announced the London route launch date, the company said it would reveal launch timings in 2027.
Qantas is planning to unveil more 20-hour direct flights from Perth in future but has abandoned references to previous hopes to run routes from Brisbane or Melbourne.
The Project Sunrise flights’ initial launch date of 2022 was delayed by the Covid-19 pandemic. Subsequent plans to start in 2025, then early 2027, were waylaid by manufacturing delays at Airbus, Qantas has said.
The company has ordered 12 Airbus A350–1000ULRs, fitted with extra fuel tanks, which can fly over 16,000km and up to 22 hours nonstop. The first is expected to arrive in Australia in April 2027.
The planes were specifically designed to fly up to 22 hours nonstop for Qantas, to complete some of the longest commercial flights in the world. A test model in July completed a 24-hour, 24-minute flight from Melbourne to Airbus’s manufacturing facility in Toulouse, France, believed to be the longest-ever commercial flight.
Each plane will contain a dedicated “wellbeing zone” between the economy and premium economy cabins, where passengers will be able to stretch, watch guided exercise videos and help themselves to snacks and drinks.
Only 140 of the A350–1000ULR’s 238 seats are standard economy. It contains six first-class suites, 52 business suites and 40 premium economy seats.
The company expects the Project Sunrise flights and sustained premium flight demand to increase its earnings by $400m over the next five years, with profit margins to rise from today’s rate of 4% to 10%.
Qantas said demand for its flights in and out of New York have doubled since 2023. Short-term US arrivals to Australia picked up 4% in the year to July 2026 compared with the year prior, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
However, Australians travelling and returning from the US dropped 9% in the same period.
Qantas’s chief executive, Vanessa Hudson, unveiled the start date at a launch party in a New York cocktail bar, as world leaders gathered in the city for the United Nations general assembly.
Hudson said the flights could change the way Australians travel.
“Reaching New York nonstop completes a vision we set out many years ago, and it’s a moment of enormous pride for the thousands of our people who have been working hard to make Project Sunrise a reality,” she said.
The company is training pilots on its A350 simulator and is teaching engineers about the new aircraft. It said more than 360 pilots and 1,200 cabin crew will be trained to operate the aircraft by the time the entire fleet has arrived.

articles.content_orig:
Twelve years after “True Detective,” Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson are reuniting on screen — as themselves.
The pair will play fictionalized versions of themselves in the new Apple TV comedy, “Brothers,” which premieres on Sept. 23.
Per Apple TV’s official synopsis, the series follows the actors as their lifelong friendship “is thrown into chaos when they uncover a decades-old secret: they might actually be brothers.”
- How to watch for free: Apple TV (one-week free trial)
- TV Channel: Streaming exclusive
“What begins as a healing getaway on McConaughey’s Texas ranch quickly spirals when Matthew’s mother, Ma Mac (Holland Taylor), accidentally lets slip a long-buried secret that the two friends might actually be brothers. As Woody turns the ranch upside down in pursuit of the truth, Matthew finds himself juggling an entirely different identity crisis: a potential run for Governor of Texas.”
In real life, McConaughey’s mother Kay admitted to being “more than friends” with Harrelson’s father, Charles Harrelson, leading to the real possibility that they could be half-brothers.
When does ‘Brothers’ come out on Apple TV?
“Brothers” premieres Wednesday, Sept. 23 with two episodes.
Apple TV has not officially confirmed a release time for episodes of “Brothers,” but the streamer will often release new episodes of original series the night before their listed premiere date. In the case of “Brothers,” you’ll likely be able to stream new episodes as early as 9:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday nights going forward.
How to watch ‘Brothers’ for free on Apple TV
“Brothers” is airing exclusively on Apple TV, so you’ll need a subscription to watch the show.
Apple TV offers a seven-day free trial for users, so you’ll be able to watch two weeks of doubleheaders before $12.99/month payments kick in.
Amazon Prime members can also subscribe to Apple TV directly through Prime Video. It costs the same monthly price and also includes a seven-day free trial, but allows you to stream Apple’s content inside the Prime Video app.
In addition to McConaughey and Harrelson starring as themselves, here’s who you’ll see on screen in “Brothers.”
- Holland Taylor as Ma Mac
- Natalie Martinez as Valentina McConaughey
- Brittany Ishibashi as Joy Harrelson
“Brothers” will have eight episodes. Check out the official Wednesday release dates for every episode below, but remember, they may be available to stream around 9:00 p.m. ET the night before the listed date.
- Episode 1: “On the Road” – Sept. 23

articles.title_orig: US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark
articles.title_zh: US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark
articles.content_orig:
US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark
The US, Denmark and Greenland have signed a defence deal that allows Washington to build two new military bases in the Arctic territory, while reaffirming Copenhagen's sovereignty over it.
Before a signing ceremony at the UN General Assembly in New York, US President Donald Trump said "we will immediately begin the process of developing a large military presence in the appropriate locations".
Danish PM Mette Frederiksen said the deal was "good for the US, Denmark and Greenland" and also for Europe and Nato, while Greenland's PM Jens-Frederik Nielsen said it was a "win-win-win".
The three leaders then inked the deal, seemingly ending more than a year of tension over the Arctic territory.
Trump had threatened to "take" the semi-autonomous Arctic territory over what he said were national security concerns, citing its strategic defence location and its mineral wealth.
His rhetoric prompted outcry from Greenlanders, Danes and European leaders who issued a joint statement saying his words "undermine transatlantic relations and risk a dangerous downward spiral".
The deal amends and updates a 1951 defence agreement between Denmark and the US.
The new pact says the US "shall be allowed to establish an additional Defence Area at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig" - referring to locations in Greenland's south and east.
Narsarsuaq is a former civilian airport and World War Two base. It has deep-water access and a large runway which US military engineers were recently surveying, the US North Command confirmed to the BBC.
The Mestersvig outpost is remote, far less developed, and used by a Danish naval dog sled unit.
The "modalities and technical details" of the bases are yet to be confirmed, and according to the deal, must be mutually agreed by all parties,
This means the US security arrangements are not unfettered and Greenland and Denmark's approval is still needed.
Washington currently operates its Pituffik Space Base in Greenland's north-west, and the new deal allows the US to "modernise and expand its activities" there.
It also says that "no state that is not a member of Nato shall be allowed to establish its own manned or unmanned military installations in Greenland nor shall they be allowed a persistent presence of military forces in Greenland".
Although the militaries of non-Nato countries are now explicitly barred from the island, it was highly unlikely that non-allied troops would have been allowed access in the first place.
Critically, no territory is ceded to the US, and it recognises both Denmark's "sovereignty and territorial integrity" and Greenland's right to self-determination.
On one hand, that's a significant climb down from Trump's earlier calls to acquire the Arctic island.
But it does deliver a strengthened US military presence and expand on the previous agreement. Therefore to some American eyes, that will be perceived as a historic win.
The new deal must still be approved by both Denmark's and Greenland's parliaments.
Despite months of crisis, the mood at Tuesday's signing ceremony appeared strikingly upbeat and friendly.
"We going to have a tremendous relationship, a secure relationship," Trump said.
"This is tremendous for Europe and for the United States, for everybody, and for Greenland it's going to be incredible."
Meanwhile, Frederiksen described the signing of the deal as a "milestone in our long-standing co-operation".
"Seventy-five years ago we entered into an agreement about the defence of Greenland. Today, we're signing an even bigger and better agreement - a deal that can last forever."
The Danish prime minister stressed that the agreement "respects sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark, as well as Greenland's right to self-determination".
Jens-Frederik Nielsen said that "for Greenland, it is not only an agreement about us, it is [an] agreement with us.
"It takes into account the people of Greenland, our rights, our livelihoods and the development of our country.
"Greenland matters for North American security and for transatlantic security," he said, adding that the Nato had a key role to play in the North Atlantic in a changing security situation.
The agreement also confirmed Greenland would remain in Nato if it were to gain independence from Denmark.
The 1951 agreement already allowed the US to send as many troops as it wanted to Greenland. Washington already has more than 100 military personnel permanently stationed at its Pituffik base.
Trump had tried for months to purchase or annex Greenland, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.
He argued the Arctic island was an essential piece of his plan to build a futuristic "Golden Dome" defence system to protect the US against missile attacks.
However the deal only mentions the project once, and contains no concrete proposal.
A Nato spokesperson said shortly afterwards that the military alliance welcomed the deal, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region".
In Denmark, the deal is being hailed as a triumph of diplomacy, and several political parties in Denmark have already said they would back it.
For Greenland, a country of 56,000 people, there was good reason for a big sigh of relief. Its leader sat side-by-side with the world's most powerful man, and got a deal that should now bring an end to months of crisis.

articles.content_orig: President Trump took his “America First” foreign policy to the world stage, using his address to the UN General Assembly to defend the war with Iran and issue a stark warning to Iran's leadership. Trump said a deal could come after the midterm elections and that the alternative was to “annihilate the Islamic Republic.” Nick Schifrin reports. President Trump took his America first foreign policy to the world stage today, using his address to the U.N. General Assembly to defend the war with Iran and issue a stark warning to Iran's leadership. Mr. Trump said a deal could come after the midterm elections, and that the alternative was to -- quote -- "annihilate the Islamic Republic." The president's speech and several of his meetings today were broadcast by the U.N.'s TV operation, which is separate from the U.S. pool of TV networks that is suing the president over his ban of three news organizations. Nick Schifrin starts our coverage from New York. Nick Schifrin: Today, in front of global leaders whose countries have been hit by unprecedented attacks, food shortages and higher energy prices because of the U.S. Israeli war in Iran, President Trump defended his decision to go to war. President Donald Trump: They were the bully of the Middle East, but they're the bully no more. Nick Schifrin: And at the U.N., whose charter bans countries from threatening military force except in self-defense, President Trump delivered a threat. Donald Trump: Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations? But I believe we will make a deal right after the election, because it doesn't make sense for them not to. Nick Schifrin: For his part today, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran did not trust another negotiation, even though Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met today with U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Masoud Pezeshkian, Iranian President (through interpreter): We have been at the negotiating table several times. The whole world sees that they are easily trample on, the agreements. They cannot use force to compel people to submit. Nick Schifrin: But President Trump's threats of force against a NATO treaty ally led to today's agreement between the U.S., Denmark, and Greenland, which has been part of the Kingdom of Denmark since 1721. The deal allows the U.S. to add to its existing military presence with two new bases. NATO will boost presence in the Arctic, and the world's largest island will permanently ban Chinese and Russian investment without giving up Greenland or Danish sovereignty. Donald Trump: We're going to have a tremendous relationship, a secure relationship, and we look forward to it. Nick Schifrin: That's a turnaround from his previous threats disrespecting Danish sovereignty that threatened overall NATO cohesion. Donald Trump: And all we're asking for is to get Greenland, including right, title and ownership, because you need the ownership to defend it. You can't defend it on a lease. Nick Schifrin: But, today, Denmark and Greenland call this deal a win-win. Mette Frederiksen, Prime Minister of Denmark: The, day we are signing an even bigger and better agreement, a deal that can last forever. This deal is good for the United States. It's good for Greenland, for Denmark, for the NATO alliance, and therefore also good for Europe. Jens-Frederik Nielsen, Prime Minister of Greenland: This is not only an agreement about us, it is an agreement with us. It takes into account the people of Greenland, our rights, our livelihoods, and the development of our country. Nick Schifrin: President Trump also met with Middle Eastern allies as the conflict with Iran has spread, this strike by the Iranian-backed Houthis on a public market in Yemen. The Houthis are trying to expand their assault after seizing the Red Sea coast along the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Regional officials are concerned the Houthi campaign gives Iran even more leverage, combining choke holds over both the Bab al-Mandab and the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis have also damaged a critical Saudi pipeline that the kingdom signaled today it's close to restarting. The president's positivity left it to outgoing Secretary General Antonio Guterres to acknowledge a world that feels fractured. Antonio Guterres, United Nations Secretary-General: The fault lines in our world are widening. Cracks have become canyons. Nick Schifrin: Today was Guterres' final U.N. General Assembly speech after a decade in office. He said challenges from climate change to AI require an interdependent world to avoid fragmentation and free-for-all. Antonio Guterres: Building a networked future begins with the recognition, especially by superpowers that their power isn't so super, and governments with the greatest AI capabilities have the greatest responsibilities to humanity to establish channels for dialogue, transparency, trust, and cooperation, not despite geopolitical rivalry, but precisely because of it. Maria Ressa, CEO, Rappler: We cannot just keep raising the alarm. We have to act. Nick Schifrin: A U.N. independent panel also warned in a new report about AI threats. But if the world came here hoping Washington would rein in AI, President Trump made clear it wouldn't be him. Donald Trump: The very same people who said we will all be dead in 12 years because of global warming, these are the same people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us all, that robots are going to attack us, and that everything is going to be a total disaster. So we're going to encourage it, not rein it in. Nick Schifrin: And, tomorrow, the Security Council will hold a meeting about artificial intelligence with foreign ministers with addresses by both American and Chinese AI leaders -- Geoff. Geoff Bennett: And, Nick, beyond what you have laid out in your report, the president today also offered his vision for Latin America? What is it? Nick Schifrin: One in which the U.S. has unvarnished military, economic, and diplomatic power. Today, he said that the drug cartels across the region were -- quote -- "the ISIS of the Western Hemisphere." He predicted also that Cuba will fall. U.S. officials tell me that there's a race between the U.S. and Cuba. The U.S. is trying to impose enough pressure on Cuba to open up economically, to change politically, while Cuba is trying to wait out, to outlast President Trump. And, tonight, President Trump will meet with Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodriguez. Today, the president was unabashed about the U.S. exporting Venezuela to the U.S., despite the Geneva Convention explicitly prohibiting nations from using war to -- quote -- "pillage the country's economic resources." Donald Trump: It was a war, but it's perhaps the biggest deal ever made. To the victor belong the spoils. Geoff Bennett: And, Nick, shifting our focus back to Yemen now, what are officials telling you about how the Houthis can be stopped? And you have some new reporting? Nick Schifrin: Yes, Geoff, it's a really big challenge. The Houthis have recently swept through the Red Sea coast right along the Bab al-Mandab. And anti-Houthi forces, including the Yemeni government, the internationally recognized Yemeni government, didn't put up much of a fight. The Saudis have launched airstrikes on the Houthis, but they have not been effective. And now the Houthis are trying to expand their control further east. A senior U.S. official tells me that President Trump is determined not to launch U.S. airstrikes on the Houthis, despite a request to do so by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, although, late last week, he did order the military to do an assessment about U.S. airstrikes, leading some in the military to suggest that they thought airst

articles.title_orig: Motorola's new Signature 27 is among the first smartphone to use the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor
articles.title_zh: Motorola's new Signature 27 is among the first smartphone to use the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor
articles.content_orig:
Motorola's new Signature 27 is among the first smartphone to use the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor
It also has Bang & Olufsen speakers.
Motorola just revealed the Signature 27 smartphone at the Snapdragon Summit. This is a refresh of the pre-existing Signature handset. The big news? It features the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 mobile processor. It's one of the first phones to use Qualcomm's latest and greatest mobile SoC.
This is a flagship model that Motorola is calling "the most advanced smartphone" it has ever created. There's some Bang & Olufsen speakers, and an upgraded cooling system to ensure the components don't get too hot.
The primary camera looks to be relatively unchanged, as it uses a 50MP Sony Lytia 910 sensor. However, the telephoto lens has gotten a major boost, up to 200MP from 50MP.
The Signature 27 runs Android 17, with a promise of seven years of OS upgrades, and provides access to plenty of Gemini-adjacent AI tools. This includes the video generator Omni and the music generator Lyria.
There's plenty we don't know here, including display specs. Motorola hasn't announced an actual release date, saying it's "expected to come to markets worldwide in 2026." We also don't know the price. The previous model costs anywhere from $800 to $1,200 or so, depending on the configuration.
We do know that this won't be the last Motorola product to feature audio by Bang & Olufsen. The companies just announced a multi-year partnership.

articles.title_orig: Egypt, China unearth wine press at temple to ancient goddess
articles.title_zh: Egypt, China unearth wine press at temple to ancient goddess
articles.content_orig:
A limestone structure believed to have once served as a wine press was recently unearthed at the Temple of Sekhmet site near the village of Mit Rahina, the Egyptian Tourism and Antiquities Ministry announced earlier this month.
Mit Rahina is located near the ancient ruins of Memphis, which in antiquity had served as the capital of the first nome of Lower Egypt.
In ancient Egyptian mythology, Sekhemet is considered both a warrior goddess and a goddess of medicine. Her temple makes up one part of the Great Temple of Ptah complex, which served as the main temple of ancient Memphis.
Discovered by a joint Egyptian-Chinese archaeological mission, the wine press includes an upper basin sloping downward toward a central opening and a lower collection basin, each topped with an opening designed to hold amphorae.
Archaeologists found grape seeds inside the press, supporting the archaeologists’ interpretation.
Dr. Hisham El-Leithy, Secretary-General of the Supreme Council of Antiquities, explained that the mission began its work by cleaning and documenting the Temple of Sekhmet as part of its excavations to understand how the site was used throughout the ages.
Mudbrick residential complex also unearthed
Additionally, the mission found the remains of a mudbrick residential complex in the area surrounding the temple, along with a series of stone blocks and statue fragments believed to have been part of Ptah’s temple.
Most of the blocks and fragments date back to the New Kingdom period, mainly during the reign of King Ramesses II, and are made from various types of stone, including limestone, red granite, and schist
Other artifacts found at the site include pottery shards, faience amulets, small terracotta and limestone statuettes, ostraca, and votive stelae.
Mohamed Abdel-Badie, head of the Egyptian Antiquities Sector at the Supreme Council of Antiquities, explained that these discoveries indicate that there had been continuous human settlement in the area between the Third Intermediate Period and the Late Period, through the Ptolemaic era and up to the Greco-Roman period.
Egypt’s Tourism and Antiquities Minister Sherif Fathy expressed his pleasure at the collaboration between Egypt and China, two of the oldest civilizations in history.
The Temple of Sekhmet was discovered by chance in 1959, during the construction of a house in the area. Following this, Egyptian antiquities inspector Mohamed Abdel Tawab El-Hetta carried out a single season of excavations at the site from 1961 to 1962.
In 2015, the visible remains of the temple were documented as part of the Ancient Memphis Site and Community Management Project.
Deity-inscribed tombstones, sarcophagi unearthed at ancient Egyptian burial site
Earlier this summer, some 20 limestone tombstones, several sarcophagi, and a collection of funerary amulets were discovered during excavations at the Tell El Deir archaeological site.
The sides and backs of the tombstones are decorated with religious symbols and godly imagery, including that of a griffin, Agathodaemon, and Isis-Thermouthis.
Agathodaemon is a lesser serpent demon in ancient Graeco-Egyptian religion, as well as in classical Greek mythology. Isis-Thermouthis is a combination of the Egyptian goddess Isis, the sister and wife of Osiris, and Renenutet (Thermuthis), the Egyptian goddess of grain.
The appearance of the two deities on the tombstones points to joint Greek and Roman influence on ancient Egyptian heritage and funerary practices.
Further, the decorations allow archaeologists to identify the social status of the tombstones’ owners.
Additionally, the Egyptian archaeological mission operating at the site uncovered a collection of pottery incense burners, decorated lamps, and funerary amulets, as well as several barrel-shaped anthropoid ceramic coffins.

articles.title_zh: Why Brunei prefers ‘quiet diplomacy’ over confrontation in South China Sea
articles.content_orig:
Why Brunei prefers ‘quiet diplomacy’ over confrontation in South China Sea
As a nation with a small military, Brunei would rather work with Beijing in safe zones such as peacekeeping than butt heads, analysts say
Brunei’s measured defence ties with Beijing reflect its low-key approach to South China Sea disputes, with analysts saying that goals such as peacekeeping offer the safest room for both sides to maintain diplomacy.
A meeting between Bruneian and Chinese defence officials in Beijing last week, when both nations pledged closer practical cooperation and support for regional stability, underscored that tact.
But observers also expect ties to remain modest, constrained by maritime claims and Bandar Seri Begawan’s preference for a diversified network of security partners.
Last Tuesday, Brunei Defence Minister Halbi Mohammad Yussof led a delegation to meet Chinese counterpart Admiral Dong Jun on the sidelines of the 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum.

articles.title_orig: Soybeans, planes and rare earths: What they say about fragile U.S.-China trade truce
articles.title_zh: Soybeans, planes and rare earths: What they say about fragile U.S.-China trade truce
articles.content_orig:
Soybean purchases, orders for Boeing aircraft and access to rare earths elements — three of the headline commitments underpinning the U.S.-China trade truce — are progressing at markedly different speeds ahead of the summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Washington on Thursday.
Taken together, the uneven fulfillment record suggests the truce is performing its minimal function of keeping commerce moving and discouraging renewed escalation, but there is little willingness on either side to cede strategic leverage, analysts said.
"The truce is moving fastest where it costs least," Eric Xiao, head of sales for Asia at CMC Markets, told CNBC.
The superpowers' May meeting reaffirmed Beijing's commitment to increase purchases of U.S. soybeans and buy 200 Boeing aircraft, while Chinese shipments of rare earths magnets are back underway after export controls were suspended for a 12-month period beginning last November.
But delivery across the three commitments has been uneven, and difficult to verify in some cases.
Larry Hu, head of China economics at Macquarie Group, described the recent U.S.-China relationship as a phase of détente — a cooling of tensions — driven by "a balance of vulnerability."
Both sides are "acutely aware of the other's choke points," Hu said in a note.
The détente should not be mistaken for a rapprochement, according to Wendy Cutler, vice president of the Asia Society Policy Institute.
"Each side has an interest in stability right now," Cutler told CNBC's "The China Connection" in May. "This doesn't mean we're going to become best friends, but it means we're going to coexist."
Soybeans: most visible lever
Soybeans offer the clearest numerical signal of progress across the trade commitments.
China has bought almost half its 25 million ton annual commitment after it purchased roughly one million tons from U.S. producers in a single week in September, Reuters reported.
Soybean purchases are also an important tool for signaling cooperation between the two nations.
"Things pick up a little bit before the bilateral meetings between Trump and Xi ... and then fall off again," China strategist Andy Rothman told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" in July, noting that purchases tended to cluster around key meetings.
Xiao described soybean purchases as "political trophies", but cautioned against interpreting soybean fulfillment as a direct sign of Beijing's stance on broader trade ties. "China buys them because it needs them," he said.
Soybean trade tiffs are not a recent development.
China, the world's largest soybean importer, saw U.S. soybeans plummet from 40% of total imports before Trump imposed tariffs on major Chinese goods in 2018, to 23% in the first five months of 2026.
Aircraft: slower, stickier pledge
Progress on the 200-aircraft commitment is less transparent.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer this week said roughly 140 aircraft were in a "good state," with orders for another 10 being written, according to Reuters. Customers, models and delivery timelines have not been disclosed.
Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg has also downplayed expectations for a single 200-aircraft announcement, saying individual Chinese airlines would place and announce orders at their own pace.
The pledge came with additional caveats, with Beijing's official account of the May agreement tying the purchases to U.S. guarantees over the supply of aircraft engines and parts.
Rare earths: strategic leverage remains
Beijing's fulfillment of the rare earths commitment is harder to measure, because the promise concerns reliable access rather than a specified export volume.
Chinese shipments of rare earths magnets to the U.S. recovered after earlier restrictions, but fell to 512 metric tons in August — down 20% from July and 13% from a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data reported by the Financial Times.
Uncertainty around rare earths access also persists for U.S. customers.
Some Chinese suppliers have declined U.S. orders because of geopolitical and compliance concerns, while some American companies have waited more than six months for export licenses, Reuters reported.
Rare earths' strategic importance may provide the clearest signal of each nation's stance on trade ties because of the strategic cost of making concessions over the materials, experts said.
Macquarie's Hu identified rare earths as the principal Chinese choke point, balanced against U.S. leverage in advanced semiconductors used in chipmaking.
Xiao similarly called rare earths the clearest indicator of the broader relationship, due to their importance in clean energy, advanced technology and defense.
Progression on the rare earths commitment could "anchor a durable relationship in a way that soybean and aircraft orders cannot," Xiao said.
He noted that exercising that leverage is a delicate calculation. A complete cutoff of exports would encourage the U.S. and its allies to accelerate alternative supply chains while hurting Chinese producers that depend on global electric vehicle and technology markets.
China's "strongest card, in other words, is one it cannot play in full," Xiao said.
– CNBC's Evelyn Cheng and Anniek Bao contributed to this story.

articles.title_orig: Alibaba unveils what it calls China’s most powerful chip and ambitious AI model plans
articles.title_zh: 阿里巴巴公布了其所谓的中国最强大的芯片和雄心勃勃的人工智能模型计划
articles.summary_zh: 香港——周二，中国阿里巴巴公布了新的人工智能芯片技术和更强大型号的计划，其中包括它所说的中国最强大的AI芯片。几天前，中美领导人将举行会议，预计在AI技术方面的竞争将是一个主要主题。
articles.content_orig:
HONG KONG — China’s Alibaba unveiled new artificial intelligence chip technologies and plans for more powerful models on Tuesday, including what it said was China’s most powerful AI chip, days ahead of a meeting between Chinese and U.S. leaders at which competition to lead on AI technology is expected to be a major theme.
Alibaba’s announcement came as U.S. AI leaders, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, are warning that China’s development of AI poses a threat to the United States and calling for an overall slowdown on development of the technology.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping is set to arrive in Washington on Wednesday for a state visit and meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump, at which AI, trade and tariffs are expected to be discussed.
At its annual flagship conference in Hangzhou, Alibaba rolled out a new AI chip and described its plans for the next generation of its AI model.
CEO Eddie Wu said the new Zhenwu V900 chip is the “most powerful AI chip in China today” and can deliver three times the performance of the company’s previous generation Zhenwu M890 chip.
Such chips power frontier AI model training and “inference,” a term for the calculations a trained AI uses to deliver responses to users. Alibaba’s Zhenwu chips are used in its data centers, providing computing to the company and its cloud clients.
Alibaba also said it plans to train a new AI model at the scale of five to 10 trillion parameters, a measure of an AI’s learning capacity, bringing it closer to the most advanced models from the U.S. Its latest Qwen3.8-Max model, the most powerful of its Qwen AI series models, has 2.4 trillion parameters.
Chinese AI company Moonshot says that its Kimi K3, released in July, is the world’s largest open model with 2.8 trillion parameters.
Alibaba also highlighted plans to expand the data centers that power its cloud computing business, citing “exponentially” rising demand for AI computing. The company said it expects to have over 20 gigawatts’ worth of computing by 2032.
SpaceX has approximately 1.4 gigawatts of AI computing capacity as of the middle of this year and says it aims to reach over 10 gigawatts in 2027.
Recent Chinese advancements in AI are giving Beijing more leverage in its upcoming talks with Washington, some analysts believe, as China steps up its self-reliance push even as U.S.-led export restrictions have barred it from accessing some of the world’s most cutting-edge technologies, including AI chips and chipmaking machines.
Open Chinese models, which are often more affordable than cutting-edge closed models from leading U.S. AI labs, have also been making inroads globally, including in the U.S.
Chinese technology giant Huawei last week also unveiled new chip technologies as it looks to challenge global leaders like Nvidia. Frontier AI model training in China often relies on Nvidia chips, analysts said, but Chinese-designed chips are gaining ground as Nvidia has been blocked from selling some of its most powerful AI chips to China.
“Using extra computing power to make up for chip limits helps China stay strong locally,” said Neil Shah, vice president of Counterpoint Research, a technology market research firm based in Hong Kong.
Counterpoint senior analyst Parv Sharma added that how much the AI and chipmaking gap between China and the U.S. narrows will also depend on other factors including China’s ability to advance chip foundries that manufacture them, not just chip design capabilities.
Alibaba is “mobilizing every resource” to meet customers’ demand for AI, CEO Wu said in his speech Tuesday.
Global shortages across the AI data center supply chain, for example, “are currently limiting the speed at which we can scale our compute infrastructure” for AI, he added.
Wu also likened AI growth to the industrial revolution and said “machine intelligence” will rapidly outgrow human thinking capacity.
While “machine intelligence today is not a substitute for human intelligence,” he predicted that, eventually, machines will be able to produce over 1,000 times more “thinking” than all of humanity combined, up from less than 3% currently.
articles.content_zh:
香港——周二，中国阿里巴巴公布了新的人工智能芯片技术和更强大型号的计划，其中包括它所说的中国最强大的AI芯片。几天前，中美领导人将举行会议，预计在AI技术方面的竞争将是一个主要主题。
阿里巴巴宣布这一消息之际，包括Anthropic首席执行官Dario Amodei在内的美国人工智能领导者警告称，中国的人工智能发展对美国构成威胁，并呼吁全面放缓该技术的发展。中国领导人Xi将于周三抵达华盛顿，进行国事访问，并与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普举行会晤，预计届时将讨论人工智能、贸易和关税问题。
在杭州举行的年度旗舰会议上，阿里巴巴推出了一款新的人工智能芯片，并介绍了其下一代人工智能模型的计划。首席执行官吴彦祖表示，新的真武V900芯片是“当今中国最强大的人工智能芯片”，其性能是公司上一代真武M890芯片的三倍。
这种芯片为前沿人工智能模型训练和“推理”提供了动力，“推理”是指经过训练的人工智能用来向用户提供响应的计算术语。阿里巴巴的真武芯片用于其数据中心，为公司及其云客户提供计算。
阿里巴巴还表示，计划以5到10万亿个参数的规模训练一个新的人工智能模型，这是衡量人工智能学习能力的一个指标，使其更接近美国最先进的模型。其最新的Qwen3.8-Max模型是其Qwen AI系列模型中最强大的，有2.4万亿个参数。中国人工智能公司Moonshot表示，其7月份发布的Kimi K3是世界上最大的开放模型，拥有2.8万亿个参数。
阿里巴巴还强调了扩大为其云计算业务提供动力的数据中心的计划，理由是对人工智能计算的需求呈“指数级”增长。该公司表示，预计到2032年，其计算能力将超过20吉瓦。截至今年年中，SpaceX拥有约1.4吉瓦的人工智能计算能力，并表示其目标是在2027年达到10吉瓦以上。
一些分析人士认为，中国在人工智能方面的最新进展使北京在即将与华盛顿举行的会谈中具有更大的影响力，因为中国正在加大自力更生的力度，尽管美国主导的出口限制禁止其获得一些世界最前沿的技术，包括人工智能芯片和芯片制造机器。打开Ch

articles.title_orig: How does Xi Jinping’s ‘special plane’ compare with Air Force One?
articles.title_zh: Xi的“专机”与空军一号相比如何？
articles.summary_zh: Xi的“专机”与空军一号相比如何？看看这位中国领导人的飞机，这一定会成为他华盛顿国事访问视觉编排的一部分中国领导人乘坐的这架飞机，在官方媒体和官方声明中经常被称为“转机”或“专机”，尽管两国都使用波音747进行总统旅行，但世界对它的了解仍远不及空军一号。
articles.content_orig:
How does Xi Jinping’s ‘special plane’ compare with Air Force One?
A look at the Chinese leader’s aircraft, which is bound to become part of the visual choreography of his state visit in Washington
The aircraft carrying China’s leader, often referred to in state media and official statements as a zhuan ji, or special plane, remains far less known to the world than Air Force One, despite both countries using Boeing 747s for presidential travel.
For a head of state, a presidential aircraft is more than a means of transport. Its range, on-board facilities and security systems reflect the practical demands of presidential travel and diplomatic missions, and the aircraft itself becomes part of the visual choreography of a state visit.
In one sense, it is one of the first symbols of a country to arrive in the host country, appearing in the sky before the president steps onto the tarmac.
articles.content_zh:
Xi的“专机”与空军一号相比如何？看看这位中国领导人的飞机，这一定会成为他华盛顿国事访问视觉编排的一部分中国领导人乘坐的这架飞机，在官方媒体和官方声明中经常被称为“转机”或“专机”，尽管两国都使用波音747进行总统旅行，但世界对它的了解仍远不及空军一号。
对于国家元首来说，总统专机不仅仅是一种交通工具。它的航程、机载设施和安全系统反映了总统旅行和外交使团的实际需求，飞机本身也成为国事访问视觉编排的一部分。从某种意义上说，它是一个国家抵达东道国的首批象征之一，在总统走上停机坪之前出现在天空中。

articles.title_orig: Trump tells U.N. he could ‘annihilate’ Iran but expects a deal after the midterm elections
articles.title_zh: Trump tells U.N. he could ‘annihilate’ Iran but expects a deal after the midterm elections
articles.content_orig:
In a speech to world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly, President Donald Trump defended the Iran conflict and said he was considering whether to “annihilate” the country and drive it “into hell.”
Or, he said, Iran could make a deal with the U.S. that would allow the nation to rebuild. But that won’t happen until after the midterm elections in November, Trump predicted.
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”
Trump later said U.S. envoys met with Iranian officials for three hours on the sidelines of the gathering, an unexpected development that offered a glimpse of diplomatic activity.
But Trump has repeatedly floated new attacks on Iran, even previously threatening death to the entire civilization. On Tuesday, he revived that warning at one of the most prominent platforms for world leaders, with an Iranian delegation in the audience.
“I have a big decision to make,” he said. “Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world? Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”
“Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he continued.
Most important, Trump said to applause, is ensuring that “Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.”
Iran’s nuclear potential was “the reality we had to confront,” he argued, and “a reality that far too many preferred to ignore.” Tehran has insisted its nuclear program is for civilian purposes and denied having plans to develop nuclear weapons.
The U.N. assembly comes as the Iran war is about to enter its eighth month.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the U.N. on Wednesday. Trump told Fox News that he would “probably” be open to meeting with Pezeshkian but did not announce any specifics.
Trump also highlighted peace deals he has worked on, U.S. actions in the Western Hemisphere and progress on his 20-point peace plan in the Gaza Strip.
Trump’s remarks to the assembly this year come as the U.N.’s Human Rights Council found in a report last week “reasonable grounds to believe” that the U.S. had committed war crimes during “indiscriminate attacks” against an Iranian school and a residential area in February.
The American president traditionally addresses the General Assembly each year.
During his wide-ranging speech, the president said America is “doing better than ever before,” touting the U.S. economy and his approach to immigration and artificial intelligence.
Less than a minute into his remarks, Trump called the U.S. economy “the envy of the world” and pointed to his administration’s tax policy and stock market records.
“Our economy is the envy of the world,” he said. “Our military is the most powerful on Earth. Our technology is second to none, and we are leading in virtually everything.”
Many American voters, though, don’t appear to agree. An NBC News poll conducted in September found that 56% of registered voters disapprove of the job the president is doing, and 55% said they believe his policies hurt the economy.
Gas prices remain high, sitting at an average of $4.47 per gallon, about a 50% increase since the war with Iran began. Diesel prices also spiked, affected by the Iran war as well as the war between Russia and Ukraine. Diesel hit a record $6 per gallon earlier this month before surging higher to $6.52 as of Tuesday, according to AAA.
Later, the president touted his record on immigration, tying his crackdown on the southern border to a drop in violent crime in the U.S.
“The entire world is being lifted by the wealth, strength, spirit and momentum of a newly energized and a very powerful United States of America,” he said.
While Trump declined to endorse guardrails on artificial intelligence, he did push for one change: its name.
Trump said the U.S. would refer in official documents to “superintelligence,” rather than “artificial intelligence.” The word “artificial,” Trump argued, “makes it sound fake, and it is not fake. It’s actually amazing.”
Earlier this month, industry insiders warned that artificial intelligence could lead to human extinction, potentially in the next decade.
Trump said Tuesday that he would not “stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution.”
“We’re going to encourage it, not rein it in,” he said. “We’re going to watch it closely through the Department of Justice.”
Trump has previously said that the only guardrail the U.S. needs is “a STRONG AND SMART” president.
Artificial intelligence is also expected to be a main topic of conversation during Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week.
Greenland, Ukraine and Venezuela
Trump met with several world leaders on the sidelines of the U.N. gathering, including Venezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez. It was Rodríguez’s first meeting with Trump since the U.S. captured then-Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, who are in a Brooklyn, New York, jail, awaiting trial.
Weeks ago, Trump said that the U.S. entered an agreement with Venezuela for U.S. majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of oil reserves in Venezuela.
On Tuesday, Trump called it “perhaps the biggest deal ever made,” adding: “To the victor belong the spoils.”
Trump said the Venezuela raid was “proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere,” noting U.S. attacks on drug cartels before pivoting to Cuba.
“My administration is seeking a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba,” he said, adding, “It will fall.”
In response, the Cuban delegation stood up and left the assembly hall.
Later Tuesday, Trump met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said: “I hope that we will end this war, and President Trump will help us help us end this war,” Zelenskyy said.
Trump said during his speech that the war in Ukraine would end “more quickly than people understand.”
For years, the president said he would end the war. During his 2024 presidential campaign, he said he could end the war within 24 hours or even before his presidency began.
Last week, Trump signed into law a Russian sanctions bill championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C.
He also announced that the U.S. would take over military operations and have “permanent control over security” in Greenland, in a deal signed later Tuesday with the leaders of Greenland and Denmark to try to end the tense standoff over the strategic Arctic territory.

articles.title_orig: Taiwan is watching closely as Xi and Trump meet and hopes US will keep up its arms sales
articles.title_zh: Taiwan is watching closely as Xi and Trump meet and hopes US will keep up its arms sales
articles.content_orig:
TAINAN, Taiwan (AP) — As China’s Xi Jinping arrives in Washington to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump, Taiwan expressed confidence that U.S. arms sales to the island that Beijing claims as its own will continue — despite China’s pressure.
China has pressed Washington to halt the arms sales, most prominently during a summit in May between Trump and Xi in Beijing. After that meeting, the United States paused the sale of a record-breaking $14 billion package — and Trump described arms sales to Taiwan as a “very good negotiating chip” with China.
Still, the U.S. government and Congress have “repeatedly expressed support for Taiwan’s self-defense capabilities,” Taiwanese Defense Ministry spokesperson Maj. Gen. Chiao Fu-chun told reporters in the southern city of Tainan.
“We will continue to maintain close contact with the U.S. Department of War and continue to push forward the arms procurement deal between Taiwan and the U.S., ensuring it proceeds as planned,” he added.
The U.S. is bound by its own laws to provide Taiwan — a self-ruled democracy that China sees as its own territory — with the means to defend itself. While not recognizing Taiwan as a country, the U.S. is the island’s strongest informal backer and arms provider.
Washington approved another $11 billion package for Taiwan in December.
Hours before Xi’s arrival for the three-day state visit to the U.S., Taiwan’s military on Wednesday conducted live fire drills featuring a domestically developed eight-wheeled armored vehicle, highlighting efforts to strengthen its own arms production.
Called The Cheetah, the vehicle can be fitted with a 105-millimeter (4.1-inch) cannon and can reach a maximum speed of about 100 kph (62 mph) and an operational range of about 500 kilometers (311 miles).
Taiwanese Maj. Gen. Chen Chien-chung said the vehicle can be used on various terrains and is suitable for urban warfare.
Trump has in recent years pressed Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te to dramatically increase Taiwan’s defense budget. The budget will exceed 3% of Taiwan’s gross domestic product for the first time in 2027, and Lai has pledged to get to 5% by 2030.
Mistreanu reported from Taipei, Taiwan.

articles.title_orig: Trump administration accuses banned media outlets of 'falsehoods' ahead of court hearing
articles.title_zh: Trump administration accuses banned media outlets of 'falsehoods' ahead of court hearing
articles.content_orig:
Trump administration accuses banned media outlets of 'falsehoods' ahead of court hearing
The US Justice Department has filed documents that accuse three media outlets banned from the White House of "trafficking in verifiable falsehoods" and reporting which "threatened national security" as it prepared to defend the move in court.
Last week, President Donald Trump barred CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news".
After their reporters had their passes confiscated and were denied access to the building, the three outlets jointly launched legal action, calling the move unconstitutional.
On Wednesday, a judge is set to decide whether to issue an order temporarily lifting the ban, pending a full hearing.
According to a court filing by the Justice Department in a District of Columbia court, the three outlets were issued with a list of "reporting incidents" by the White House ahead of the ban.
The filing cites a number of stories about construction at the White House - including about a security bunker and the building of a new ballroom, as well as a report on an internal information leak investigation.
It goes on to say that "access to the White House is a privilege, not a right".
The three media organisations have argued that the ban breaches their rights under the First Amendment, which forbids the government from "abridging" the freedom of the press.
In a joint statement confirming legal action against the government, they said: "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting.
"Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference."
Major TV networks have withdrawn from a media-sharing arrangement of video and images of the president, known as the pool, in protest over the ban.
Shortly after, the White House launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, which operates a 24/7 feed of clips of the president.

articles.title_orig: Digital yuan speeds up as Ant International spurs instant cross-border transfers
articles.title_zh: Digital yuan speeds up as Ant International spurs instant cross-border transfers
articles.content_orig:
Chinese banks, Ant International push instant cross-border digital yuan transfers
The Shanghai-to-Hong Kong settlements worth hundreds of millions of yuan bypassed traditional channels and could accelerate Beijing’s broader yuan strategy
Two Chinese state-owned banks and Ant International have trialled cross-border digital yuan transfers worth hundreds of millions of yuan, marking the latest step in Beijing’s efforts to streamline settlements and promote wider international use of the digital yuan.
The Shanghai branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) facilitated its first digital yuan transfer for Ant International to ICBC Asia, its Hong Kong subsidiary. The transaction from Shanghai to Hong Kong was completed within seconds, compared with the several days typically required for large cross-border transfers through traditional channels, domestic media outlet Financial News reported on Tuesday.
Ant International is the Singapore-based arm of China’s Ant Group, an affiliate of Alibaba, which owns the South China Morning Post.
Similarly, the Shanghai branch of China Construction Bank (CCB) also facilitated a digital yuan transfer worth hundreds of millions of yuan for Ant International to CCB Asia, the bank’s Hong Kong subsidiary, state-owned China Business Journal reported on Friday.

articles.title_orig: U.S. and Iran officials meet in New York to discuss ending the war
articles.title_zh: U.S. and Iran officials meet in New York to discuss ending the war
articles.content_orig:
Donald Trump Says He Could ‘Annihilate’ Iran After Touting Peace Efforts
President Donald Trump told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that he could "annihilate" Iran if the nearly seven-month war does not end in a deal, even as he cast himself as a peacemaker working to close out multiple global wars. The remarks, given in New York, came alongside a day of intense back-channel diplomacy between US and Iranian officials.
Donald Trump's Iran remarks come during United Nations speech
Trump to the UN: "Do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly? Do I drive them into hell?" pic.twitter.com/cIYBO1Mp3w
— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) September 22, 2026
Speaking before a packed hall, Trump said he faced a stark choice. "I have a big decision to make," he said. "Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?… Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell?" Only a single member of Iran's delegation was present to watch the speech.
Trump used much of his address to defend the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, arguing the war had stopped Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon and proved the value of what he called peace through strength. He also touted efforts to broker peace between Russia and Ukraine, rejected the idea of "global government," and pledged that the US would win the global race on artificial intelligence.
His tone stood in contrast to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, who had earlier warned that global divisions were increasing and stressed the interdependence of nations. According to Reuters, Iran's Armed Forces rejected Donald Trump's UN remarks as "propaganda" in a statement Tuesday, warning of "full readiness to inflict more severe, crushing, and unpredictable blows on the aggressors."
Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, who led Iran's negotiating team in earlier talks, said Tehran would not bow to pressure: "Trump must understand that he cannot impose his power on the Iranian people and its armed forces." Despite the threats exchanged publicly, US and Iranian officials continued diplomatic contacts Tuesday, including discussions through mediators and a meeting on the sidelines of the UN gathering.

AI trade outlook brightens on falling oil and Meta’s Muse agent ahead of Xi-Trump meeting
Nasdaq-100 hits record high while chip stocks in China and South Korea rebound, with investors betting that AI earnings can weather higher interest rates
The global AI trade is staging a comeback, as a confluence of falling oil prices, Meta Platforms’ launch of a new agentic tool, and anticipation surrounding the China-US leadership summit reignite interest in technology stocks.
The Nasdaq-100 Index hit an all-time high on Tuesday, surpassing the previous record set in June. In Asia, China’s chip-heavy Star Market 50 Index and South Korea’s Kospi gauge, which is heavily weighted towards memory chipmakers, have been bouncing back since July sell-offs.
The shift appears to mark a reversal in negative sentiment surrounding artificial intelligence stocks, which had been battered by inflationary fears and calls from some US tech companies to slow the development of new AI models due to safety concerns. Market sentiment pivoted as oil’s retreat below US$100 a barrel eased inflationary pressure and as Meta’s Muse agent reinforced demand across the AI supply chains.
Meanwhile, positive rhetoric from a preparatory trade talk before the sit-down between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump has fuelled optimism for a de-escalation of geopolitical tensions.

Trump Administration officials on Tuesday announced that they would terminate the Obamacare coverage of 760,000 enrollees, alleging widespread fraud in enrollment.
Vice President JD Vance, who leads a White House task force aimed at eliminating fraud, said while speaking to reporters that $2.2 billion in taxpayer funds would be saved by removing the hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act (ACA) enrollees from the public insurance marketplaces.
“We expect that most of these people are fraudulently enrolled,” Vance said. He added that the Administration would also work to verify the eligibility of roughly 419,000 additional enrollees by ensuring that they are legal residents of the U.S. and meet the income threshold to receive Obamacare coverage.
The Administration will also place a six month moratorium on new health insurance brokers and agents, who help individuals sign up for health plans, Vance said.
Read More: Trump Pledges to Issue $500 Refunds to Nearly a Million Obamacare Enrollees. Are You Eligible?
The Administration’s move to eject fraudulent enrollees from the Obamacare insurance marketplaces is the latest in its broader efforts to crack down on fraud. An online “ledger” maintained by the White House asserts that the Vance-led anti-fraud task force has uncovered nearly $250 billion worth of fraud since Trump returned to office last January, including almost $100 billion at the Department of Health and Human Services.
That crackdown also saw the Administration pause $867.5 million in Medicaid payments to California and $199 million in Minnesota in July, an action for which Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. cited “suspected fraud and noncompliance.” Both states have pushed back on the claims.
The Administration has additionally targeted alleged fraud in food stamps , childcare facilities, COVID-era relief funding, student loans, and homelessness funding, among other areas. Critics have accused it of disproportionally focusing on Democratic-led states in its crackdown.
An analysis from the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) released last August estimated that 2.3 million Obamacare enrollees improperly claimed premium tax credits by intentionally overstating their income in 2025. The Trump Administration has also claimed that agents and brokers have been responsible for illegally enrolling tens of thousands of people in ACA plans.
The 760,000 enrollees now being removed from the ACA rolls by the Trump Administration represent about 4% of the estimated 19.2 million people receiving coverage through the marketplaces in 2026.
That total has sharply declined from its peak of more than 24 million last year as ACA premiums have surged following the expiration of subsidies that helped reduce costs for millions of enrollees at the end of 2025.
A poll conducted by health policy research group KFF in June found that most voters believe there is at least some fraud in government health programs, and that more than 70% feel it is an extremely or very important issue for candidates to discuss ahead of the midterm elections. For Republican voters, fraud topped all health care issues asked about in the survey, including costs.
But health care costs, which have become increasingly expensive in the U.S. in recent years, weighed more significantly for voters overall, and the poll found that only a minority of those surveyed believed that reducing fraud in government programs would reduce such costs for them personally.
Amid the Trump Administration’s moves to withhold millions in Medicaid payments, 71% also voiced the belief that preserving access to coverage through the insurance program was more important than rooting out fraud. Meanwhile, 65% believed that the Administration’s Medicaid payment deferrals were mostly politically motivated.

Men’s title a landmark achievement for China, with success marking the 200th gold in athletics at the regional multi-sport event
China’s racewalkers secured a landmark gold as they dominated the half marathons at the Asian Games on Wednesday, winning both the men’s and women’s events.
A new distance compared to the 20km version contested at previous Asian Games, Shi Shengji stormed to the men’s title at the Aichi-Nagoya race walking course in one hour, 23 minutes and 32 seconds.
The 19-year-old from Jiangsu built up a commanding lead of almost four and a half minutes over world and Asian double-record holder Toshikazu Yamanishi of Japan, who finished in 1:28:01.
Choe Byeong-kwong of South Korea took bronze in 1:28:35, while Hongkonger Chin Man-kit finished fifth out of nine contestants, crossing the line in 1:34:26. China’s Li Chenjie was disqualified.

“With the security environment becoming increasingly severe, including in Asia, the fact that Donald and I are holding talks here at U.N. headquarters today demonstrates the strength of the Japan-U.S. alliance to the world,” Takaichi said ahead of their 35-minute, closed-door meeting.
