articles.title_orig: China’s surging biotech sector represents both competition and lifeline for the US
articles.title_zh: China’s surging biotech sector represents both competition and lifeline for the US
articles.content_orig:
As Chinese companies push beyond “me-too” drugs and the country lays out a new five-year plan targeting a $522 billion–strong biotech industry by 2030, experts say more predictable funding and regulation could help the U.S. maintain its edge.
Emerging from stealth earlier this month, Boston-based Solstice Oncology highlighted its origins in a trans-Pacific exchange that’s grown commonplace. The startup licensed its lead asset, colon cancer candidate porustobart, from Chinese biotech Harbour BioMed in February in a deal worth more than $100 million upfront and potentially upwards of $1 billion. Such deals are helping to fuel the rapid growth of Chinese biotech, which is also the beneficiary of decades of focused support by its government.
There’s ample reason to believe that trend will continue: Last week, the Chinese government released a new five-year plan that lays out a goal of $521.8 billion in combined revenue for its domestic biotech industry by 2030. It also aims to originate at least 25% of first-in-class drugs on the global market by that date.
Meanwhile, out-licensing from Chinese biotechs has surged since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, from 35 such deals worth a total of $989 million in 2019 to 186 deals worth $137.7 billion in 2025, according to data from PharmCube. Evaluate has predicted that Chinese assets will make up more than two-thirds of total deal value this year, up from less than 5% five years ago.
“The number of licensing deals have radically accelerated, wherein large pharmaceutical companies are increasingly turning their business development to China,” Jeremy Levin, executive chairman of Ovid Therapeutics, told BioSpace. “The shift of pharmaceutical licensing activity toward China-originated assets is now an established fact, and two years ago it was far less pronounced.”
Such licensing deals may be a boon to companies like Solstice Oncology, but the rise of Chinese biotech has prompted considerable handwringing about U.S. competitiveness.
“We have to start thinking about what it means if we so erode our innovation base here in the U.S. that we are dependent on a potential adversary for life-sustaining medications,” Caitlin Frazer, executive director of the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology (NSCEB), told BioSpace last month.
The Chinese government’s prioritization of biotech traces back to a 2006 mention of related terms in a medium- and long-term planning document, said Alexander Brown, a senior analyst at the Mercator Institute for China Studies (MERICS). The sector has continued to crop up in government planning documents in the two decades since. While experts say it’s difficult to quantify how much the Chinese government puts into its domestic biotech sector, Brown and a MERICS co-author estimated the investment was at least 20 billion renminbi (about $3 billion) in 2023.
One difficulty in quantifying the government’s support is that it goes beyond direct investment in startups, Cyriac Roeding, CEO of the cancer therapeutics firm Earli, said in an interview. “The Chinese government does a lot of things in many different ways, not just direct investments, but also purchases, like getting into the game as a customer, or cheaper supplies,” he explained.
Levin said the Chinese government’s biotech strategy has taken decades to execute. First, it established the ability to manufacture medications. Next came domestic contract research organizations (CROs). “That gave them the ability to make a molecule and then to test it,” Levin said. “As they did that, they studied very carefully how we approved drugs. And so they established and continually refined their drug approval process in China.”
In step three, China launched clinical trials “in a way that complemented their testing of drugs in the CRO-like environment,” Levin said. “They established a highway which was high speed for the development of so-called lookalikes or bio-betters,” medications based on the mechanism of action of existing drugs developed elsewhere. In step four, the government launched programs aimed at attracting researchers who’d gained valuable training and experience abroad to return and put their skills to work domestically. These programs cover a range of science and engineering fields in addition to biotech.
Some commenters have used the specter of Chinese competition to argue for more streamlined regulation of clinical trials in the U.S. On the flip side of the same coin, two lawmakers called for increased FDA oversight of Chinese study sites and scrutiny of data collected there after several clinical trial deaths in the country. But none of the experts who spoke with BioSpace cited a superior regulatory process as a factor in the rise of the Chinese biotech industry.
“Yes, [regarding the] FDA, there’s a lot of things that can be done better. No question,” Roeding said. But that’s not going to reorient the trajectories of the U.S. and Chinese biotech sectors. Rather, he argued, you have to follow the money.
Roeding pointed out that the billions poured into licensing deals with Chinese companies represent money not going to innovative early-stage research happening stateside. That compounds what he sees as the major factor holding U.S. biotech back as China rises: a lack of consistent funding.
While he conceded that boom and bust cycles have always characterized private investment in U.S. biotech, he said funding for early-stage, innovative research is far worse than in the past because of a prolonged post-COVID bust and because AI ventures are now attracting the vast majority of venture capital investment, leaving little leftover for biotech. And while currently the “XBI looks great,” Roeding said, most investment that does reach biotech goes to clinical-stage companies rather than earlier-stage work.
“This industry is deeply suffering from the lack of consistency. That’s our biggest problem,” Roeding said. “Consistent funding for innovation that has long cycles of time, much longer than others, is critical.”
To accomplish that, he argues for the creation of a publicly funded sovereign wealth fund. Its investments should be concentrated in bust cycles and in bridging the “valley of death” between early, NIH-funded research and clinical validation, he said. “And now you can start flattening the [boom-and-bust investment] curve and you can be internationally competitive.”
Moreover, Roeding added, “the beautiful thing about it is if it’s done right. . . . It’s actually going to pay itself back and more. Society is going to make money off this.”
Levin has a different take. A lack of appreciation for biotech and a failure to differentiate it from pharma mean that the former sector suffers from price-control policies such as the IRA and Most Favored Nation, as well as a health insurance industry that often pushes the cost of drugs onto patients, he said.
Then to add insult to injury, Levin continued, the FDA substantially reduced its workforce last year, laying off about 20% of employees. That loss of institutional knowledge caused what he called “structural damage” that risks widening an already established competitive gap as China moves rapidly in biotechnology.
That said, Chinese biotech faces barriers of its own, Levin noted, especially in their capability to scale, to fully develop drugs on their own and to reach overseas markets. “And that’s why we’re seeing a huge takeoff, also, of out-licensing deals in recent years,” Levin told BioSpace.
“So it’s not all rosy for the Chinese biotech sector,” he continued, “but certainly this long-term government backing and just the fact that they’re able to do research and do certain processes in China at a higher scale, at a cheaper cost, at a faster speed than in other countries is really a core reason why they’re rising so quickly.”

articles.title_orig: Live updates: Trump says he faces a decision on Iran to make a deal or ‘annihilate’ the country
articles.title_zh: 实时更新：特朗普表示，他面临着就伊朗达成协议或“消灭”该国的决定
articles.summary_zh: •特朗普演讲：美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在联合国大会上表示，中期选举后与伊朗达成协议是可能的，但他的另一个选择是“消灭伊斯兰共和国”。他还谈到了美国的军火库存以及在格兰岛建立“大规模军事存在”的计划。当他发誓古巴共产党政府“会垮台”时，古巴代表团退出了。
articles.content_orig:
• Trump speech: US President Donald Trump told the UN General Assembly a deal with Iran is possible after the midterm elections, but his other choice is to “annihilate the Islamic Republic.” He also spoke about US munitions stockpiles and plans to establish a “large military presence” on Greenland. When he vowed that Cuba’s communist government “will fall,” the Cuban delegation walked out.
• Iran talks: President Masoud Pezeshkian has landed in New York to attend the General Assembly, Iranian state media reported. Earlier today, the US and Iranian delegations engaged in “lengthy talks” through mediators, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said.
• Meeting with Zelensky: Meanwhile, Trump said he thinks Ukraine and Russia will make a deal but did not give any specifics. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky separately said he is ready for a trilateral meeting with Russia and the US.
Venezuela's acting leader hails first meeting with Trump since Maduro capture
Acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez hailed her first meeting with US President Donald Trump since the US captured her predecessor Nicolás Maduro as “historic.”
“We discussed strengthening the bilateral relationship between our countries and advancing a cooperation agenda in strategic areas such as energy, mining, and security,” Rodríguez said in a post on X late Tuesday, alongside a photo of the two.
Rodríguez, who spoke to Trump on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, thanked the US President for support during the devastating earthquakes that hit Venezuela in June.
“We will continue to advance a diplomacy that serves the national interest, aimed at achieving concrete results and collective benefits for the Venezuelan people,” she added.
CNN has reached out to the White House for comment on the meeting.
Trump met with Venezuela's acting leader as country carries out US-backed reforms
US President Donald Trump met tonight with acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez as Washington maintains political pressure on her country to enact reforms.
The meeting, which Rodríguez confirmed on X late Tuesday evening, comes more than eight months after the US captured Rodríguez’s predecessor, strongman leader Nicolás Maduro, in a daring operation in Venezuela.
Maduro is currently being held in a Brooklyn detention center, just miles from the UN General Assembly.
Since Maduro’s capture, the US has compelled Rodríguez’s acting government to open Venezuela’s oil industry to foreign investment, release hundreds of political prisoners, roll back ties with US adversaries such as Cuba, and reestablish diplomatic ties with the US.
Washington says the goal is for Venezuela to eventually transition into a democracy, though Trump has repeatedly said the country isn’t ready for elections yet, and Human Rights Watch says the country still needs institutional reforms to protect people’s basic rights.
During the transition process, the US has largely sidelined Venezuela’s opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, who won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize for promoting democratic rights in the country.
Some of the global leaders who will be speaking at UNGA this week
The speeches delivered from the United Nations General Assembly podium often attract attention for the behavior of the audience as much as the speakers themselves.
Last year, numerous delegates left the auditorium while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke. In 2018, laughing delegates interrupted US President Donald Trump’s speech as he outlined his administration’s achievements.
One big question is whether Chinese leader Xi Jinping will make a surprise appearance in New York. Xi is due to appear in Washington for a state visit while the General Assembly is underway.
Other headline speakers include Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who spoke first Tuesday, and Netanyahu, who will speak Thursday, according to a preliminary list.
Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodríguez will make her UN debut on Wednesday while her former boss, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, sits in jail mere miles away in Brooklyn.
Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas is slotted for a Thursday speaking time before Netanyahu. However, the Trump administration has again refused Abbas a visa, so he will almost certainly address the chamber via video.
Even as it denies visas to Palestinian officials, the administration will allow Iran’s “core delegation,” which would likely include President Masoud Pezeshkian, to come to New York.
Pezeshkian speaking in New York while his country is actively engaged in combat with the United States is virtually unprecedented. The closest international equivalent might be Egyptian President Anwar Sadat’s 1977 visit to Israel while the two countries were technically at war — but even that was part of a larger peace process.
The role UNGA has played in global events
All eyes are on New York this week as world leaders gather for a high-level meeting of the UN General Assembly, the organization’s main policymaking body, where all its member states are represented. Historically, the assembly has passed some landmark resolutions but its impact has lessened in recent years.
In 1948, member states adopted both the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Genocide Convention, providing the basis for modern international human rights law. Later, in 1956, the assembly established the first ever UN peacekeeping force during the Suez Canal Crisis to supervise the withdrawal of French, British and Israeli troops from Egypt.
The assembly also approved the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) in 1968, which aimed to stop more countries developing nuclear weapons. Almost every country joined except Israel, India and Pakistan, while North Korea withdrew from the treaty in 2003, displaying the UN’s limited ability to compel countries to stick to its resolutions. And in 1996, UNGA adopted the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty, helping to almost completely curb the practice.
More recently, however, its resolutions have become less concrete in nature. The assembly endorsed the Responsibility to Protect doctrine in 2005 and established the Human Rights Council in 2006. In 2015 it adopted the Sustainable Development Goals seeking to end poverty, turbocharge climate action and reduce inequality, but progress has been slow in some areas and non-existent in others.
Here’s what world leaders focused on in their General Assembly speeches today
Emmanuel Macron gave his last speech to the United Nations General Assembly as the French president and the United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham gave his first.
Here are the highlights from the key speeches today:
- Trump: The US president said he has a “big decision” to make on Iran, framing the choice as reaching a deal after the midterm elections or annihilating the country.
- Macron: While President Donald Trump described the International Court of Justice as “evil,” Macron said France would continue to support the court. The French president also called for a“double moratorium” on strikes on energy infrastructure and shipping through the Black Sea amid the Russia-Ukraine war. He also condemned violence in the occupied West Bank, as well as a lack of lasting peace in Gaza.
- Burnham: In his inaugural speech, the prime minister put his support behind AI, saying it “brings together so many of the most pressing issues before us.” The prime minister praised AI for its potential to transform healthcare and education and for being “the key to economic growth,” while acknowledging mounting security concerns.
There were also a lot of notable meetings and announcements on the sidelines of the event. Here’s the key things to know:
- Trump and Burnham: They bonded over their shared hope for Britain’s future, and the prime minister said they discussed the Middle East, the Falkland Islands and trade issues, Reuters reported.

•会见泽连斯基：与此同时，特朗普表示，他认为乌克兰和俄罗斯将达成协议，但没有给出任何具体细节。乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基分别表示，他已准备好与俄罗斯和美国举行三方会谈。
特朗普会见委内瑞拉代理领导人，委内瑞拉正在进行美国支持的改革
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普今晚会见了委内瑞拉代理总统德尔西·罗德里格斯，因为华盛顿继续对委内瑞拉施加政治压力，要求其实施改革。
罗德里格斯于周二晚间X证实了这次会议，八个多月前，美国在委内瑞拉的一次大胆行动中抓获了罗德里格斯的前任、强人领袖尼古拉斯·马杜罗。
马杜罗目前被关押在布鲁克林拘留中心，距离联合国大会仅几英里。
自马杜罗被捕以来，美国迫使罗德里格斯的代理政府向外国投资开放委内瑞拉的石油工业，释放数百名政治犯，撤销与古巴等美国对手的关系，并重建与美国的外交关系。
华盛顿表示，目标是委内瑞拉最终过渡到民主国家，尽管特朗普一再表示该国尚未为选举做好准备，人权观察组织表示，该国仍需要进行体制改革以保护人民的基本权利。
在过渡过程中，美国在很大程度上排挤了委内瑞拉反对派领导人玛丽亚·科琳娜·马查多，她因促进该国的民主权利而获得2025年诺贝尔和平奖。

articles.title_orig: Missouri’s embattled, Trump-backed congressional map returns to Supreme Court for a third time
articles.title_zh: Missouri’s embattled, Trump-backed congressional map returns to Supreme Court for a third time
articles.content_orig:
A quixotic legal battle over whether Missouri may use a GOP-friendly congressional redistricting plan for November’s election returned to the Supreme Court for the third time late Tuesday night, forcing the justices to once again review an effort the court unanimously rejected less than two weeks ago.
The emergency appeal will — once again — decide if Republicans can flip an additional House seat in the November midterm election. It’s also part of an extraordinary push by Republicans to continue to fight for the seat after the conservative high court has signaled it is uninterested in getting involved in the messy, months-old dispute over the state’s map.
A group opposed to the map filed the emergency case at the Supreme Court late Tuesday a day after a federal appeals court ruled that Missouri must use the Republican-friendly map in November, rather than a map created in 2022, because voters had already selected nominees based on the newer map in the state’s primary election.
“Ballots using the 2022 map have been printed and mailed, and absentee voting, both by mail and in-person, began today,” the group told the Supreme Court in its appeal. “Those ballots cannot be reassigned to new districts now.”
Justice Brett Kavanaugh, who handles appeals arising from Missouri, requested a response in the case by Wednesday afternoon.
Missouri’s new map targeted the 5th Congressional District, held by Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver, by breaking up its Kansas City base and stretching it into rural and Republican-leaning parts of the state. There would be seven conservative-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning, a change from the current 6-2 split.
The whipsaw case of Missouri’s congressional map may be merely an appetizer for the banquet of election appeals that are likely to reach the justices tied to this year’s midterms.
The justices have already shut down an effort by President Donald Trump to give the US Postal Service more power to screen mail ballots. The court has also already juggled a series of other redistricting disputes this year, including in Texas, California, Louisiana, Alabama and Virginia.
University of Chicago law professor William Baude said Tuesday that it was “a hundred to one” likely that the court would reject the GOP map again. He described the case as a “taste of what’s to come.”
The Missouri Supreme Court ruled earlier this month that the 7-1 Republican map adopted by the legislature at Trump’s behest last year could not be used because of a referendum challenge brought against it under the state constitution. State Republicans challenged that, appealing all the way up to the US Supreme Court. Kavanaugh, a conservative, declined that request, which appeared to settle the matter.
But minutes after that decision, a federal district court stepped in with a ruling in favor of the GOP map. And the case was once again appealed to the US Supreme Court, which once again sided against reviving the GOP map. In that instance, the full court reviewed the case, and no justices noted their dissent. The court also did not explain its reasoning.
The conservative 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals read the boilerplate language from the Supreme Court, and its lack of reasoning, as an invitation to rush through its own ruling. In an unsigned opinion, the court concluded that “the Constitution does not permit Missouri to use a different congressional district map in the November 2026 general election than it used in the August 2026 primary election.” And it ordered a federal trial court to once again require that the state move forward with the 7-1 map.
It is that decision that has prompted the third round of appeals.
Even though the 8th Circuit ruled in favor of the GOP, it ordered the lower court to pause the impact of that decision until Monday to give the appeals a chance to play out. That means the Supreme Court is likely to either settle the dispute before Monday, or issue a short-term extension of that deadline to give the justices more time to decide.
CNN’s Tierney Sneed contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: A lot’s changed since Xi Jinping’s last US state visit. Mostly in China’s favor.
articles.title_zh: A lot’s changed since Xi Jinping’s last US state visit. Mostly in China’s favor.
articles.content_orig:
When Chinese leader Xi Jinping visits Washington this week, he will be sitting down with President Donald Trump in a vastly different position than the last time the two men met face-to-face in the United States nearly a decade ago.
At that 2017 summit at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort China was lagging America on multiple fronts and vulnerable to the tech and trade frictions Trump would unleash on it in the coming year.
Now, Xi arrives at the helm of a country that’s transformed.
The world’s second largest economy has emerged as a tech heavyweight. Home-grown tech talent is spurring Chinese AI models ever closer to Silicon Valley’s frontier. Beijing-based space firms are launching and landing reuseable rockets with their sights on global champion SpaceX. Companies from energy to AI, robots and memory chips have launched blockbuster stock debuts over the past year.
China’s manufacturing juggernaut racked up a $1.2 trillion global trade surplus last year, due in part to surging demand for its electric vehicles, solar panels and chips. Its grip on the supply chains for some exports – especially rare earths – has given Beijing unique leverage over Washington and Trump’s “America First” trade war.
And at a moment when the US is antagonizing allies and has yet to find a way to end its war on Iran that’s destabilizing the global economy, Xi has been burnishing China’s image as a responsible and dependable global leader.
Throughout policy circles in Beijing, there is a consensus: gone are the days when the US could make one-directional demands of China.
“China is far more confident than nine years ago and what’s even more important is that today China has found an effective way to keep the US in check,” said Wu Xinbo, dean of the Institute of International Studies at Shanghai’s Fudan University, who advises the government on foreign policy.
“Washington has to treat Beijing with more equality, respect and this relationship has to be more and more reciprocal.”
That doesn’t mean the stakes are low for Xi as he arrives in Washington for an expected three-day stay.
The Chinese leader is banking on China’s high-tech transformation to inject momentum into a slowing economy. Maintaining “constructive strategic stability” – an ambition the two sides agreed to during a meeting in Beijing in May – could help ensure frictions or conflict with the US don’t get in the way.
But buoyed by China’s growing global and technological clout, Xi will also be presenting to the US a new reality: while Beijing wants a stable relationship with the US, its rise doesn’t depend on it.
In a bullish editorial in party mouthpiece the People’s Daily on Wednesday that helps illustrate this confidence, China’s ambassador to the US warned that Taiwan and human rights are “red lines” for Beijing that cannot be crossed.
“China’s sovereignty, security, and development interests must not be violated. The four red lines concerning the Taiwan issue, democracy and human rights, China’s political system and development path, and its right to development must not be challenged,” Xie Feng wrote.
For Xi, a key source of that confidence has been China’s ability to diversify trade away from the US market and build out its technological self-sufficiency – two mandates sharpened by pressures on China from the first Trump administration.
Beijing has funneled vast financing and political will toward building its own technology in cutting-edge sectors – like robotics, AI, biotech, space, new energy and chips – and applying that tech into industry.
The fruits of that growth, however, are not spread evenly. Youth unemployment hit a recent high last month. Hundreds of millions of workers rely on the gig economy, such as delivering food or driving ride-share cars for their primary work. Consumption lags, local governments struggle under debt and a huge property sector crisis rumbles on.
People from all walks of life in China will readily tell you that the economy is just not doing as good as it used to be. But alongside this, there is often a sense of pride that the country has been able to rise as a tech power, even in the face of US-imposed restrictions.
Look no further than the case of Huawei, the Chinese tech giant blacklisted by the first Trump administration. In recent days Chinese tech vloggers have been gleefully posting videos about Apple’s much-hyped release of its first foldable phone. They point out that Huawei’s own foldable model came out seven years ago.
Days ahead of Xi’s visit to the US, Huawei also announced that its next generation of Ascend AI chips would be released ahead of schedule next year, signaling progress in what has been a crucial bottleneck for China in AI development.
“We cannot accept a destiny where we cannot control our fate being determined by others in terms of willingness to sell chips to China or not,” Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu said earlier this month.
And while the American public is largely pessimistic about the development of AI, their peers in China are more focused on how it might impact their day-to-day lives. Job displacement is a concern, but there’s also a sense there is an opportunity to be seized – and that the ruling Communist Party, with its tight control over society, won’t let the technology spin out of control.
Xi is heading to the US in the middle of an explosion of conversation about the risks of AI, including from Chinese models. Trump has said the country can’t slow development for safety, because it must focus on beating China.
That puts the spotlight on a key aim from Xi and his delegation: to dissuade the US from more tech restrictions that further could limit Chinese firms’ access to American technology or markets.
China wants to see “greater predictability in the economic and technology relationship” and a “stronger political commitment to prevent sensitive issues — especially Taiwan and technology restrictions — from destabilizing the overall relationship,” according to Sun Chenghao, a senior fellow at Tsinghua University’s Center for International Security and Strategy in Beijing.
But this is also where the shifting balance of power between China and the US comes in.
Both sides know that new restrictions – if seen by Beijing as too aggressive – could reignite the conflict that led their economies to the brink of full decoupling last year.
The truce that ended that round of their trade war was reached only after Beijing threatened a massive expansion of export controls on strategically critical rare earths, in response to a US move that would have vastly expanded the number of blacklisted Chinese firms.
That truce will likely be extended this week – and both sides will be wary of pushing the other too far in a situation where “nobody wins, because it’s equally matched,” according to Kurt Tong, managing partner at The Asia Group advisory firm.
“In the economic space, there isn’t really any superior player … because of the equally matched leverage aspects, the two sides are pulling back from actions that cost them to execute,” said Tong, who formerly served as the US consul general of Hong Kong.
Now, Trump “looks at Xi Jinping and sees a counterpart as opposed to someone to wrestle into submission,” he said.
China is now seen more positively than the US in most of 36 countries surveyed in a new Pew Research poll published in July. Xi even edged out Trump in winning people’s confidence, the pollsters found.
These changes come not just alongside a shake-up of the role of the US on the global stage, but a shift in China’s ability to wield soft power. People around the world are using Chinese AI models for their businesses and driving Chinese EVs. Viral cultural exports like the Labubu plushy and Chinese dramas, as well as the online Chinamaxxing trend have driven interest and tourism in China.

articles.title_orig: Worries about an AI internet takeover gain new urgency among doomsday scenarios
articles.title_zh: Worries about an AI internet takeover gain new urgency among doomsday scenarios
articles.content_orig:
I visited the CEO of a major startup in SF last week. He recounted a tale that blew my mind.
His company recently put a new product online but hadn't done a big launch or any marketing. Within a week or two, it got at least a million signups. Barely any humans even knew about it. This was all AI agents just finding this new tool and using it en masse.
This is the future of the internet, and it's arriving at warp speed.
Back in early 2025, I described a vision of a "dark internet" where humans will be drowned out by agents accessing and using online information, widgets, and tools all by themselves.
Silicon Valley got busy building the "rails" for this agentic web so that these autonomous software programs could act on our behalf, executing workflows, doing online chores, and even paying for things, all without us lifting a finger.
This took a couple of years, but the early foundations have been built and that's been enough to support a sudden surge in agent activity online, producing both stunning and worrying results.
Meta recently launched a personal agent called Muse, which got busy scouring the web and calling customer service on behalf of millions of users. It hit the top of the app charts late Thursday. Instinct, an agent that lives in your text messages, is performing similar feats.
In the workplace, coding agents are churning out millions of lines of code faster than any human software engineer. And some of these bots have broken out of online testing environments, sparking new predictions of AI doom and calls for an industry slowdown.
That's unlikely to stop the agentic internet from exploding and changing how our lives and businesses are run in unprecedented ways.
Bot traffic overtook human traffic online a few months ago, and it could become 1,000 times bigger than human-generated traffic in about five years, according to Cloudflare estimates.
"Humans will be a rounding error on the internet, not because human traffic goes down, but that's just how fast we're seeing non-human traffic grow," Cloudflare CFO Thomas Seifert said earlier this year.
"AI agentic Internet traffic will obviously VASTLY exceed human usage. Not a close call at all," Elon Musk wrote on X following the Cloudflare projection.
An internet designed for machines is likely to be very different from the one that was built over the past few decades for humans.
Take a look at this video posted this week on X by Gregor Žunič, cofounder of Browser Use, a startup that's developing an AI agent framework for controlling web browsers and automating online tasks.
It shows an agent using Google to find the best flight from Zurich to London on a specific date. It took the bot seven seconds, way faster than a human could do it.
Breaking: Browser Use + Jev = Ultrafast ⚡
Findings flights took 7s and cost only $0.0039 🤯
> new action space every step
> small LLM fallback to type
(this video is at 1x speed btw)
Built a tiny open source browser agent. try it below ↓ pic.twitter.com/AplCBRYC5o
Imagine this happening millions of times a second on sites built for human, not machine, speed?
As with all powerful new technology, the agentic internet will produce good and bad outcomes. And we're already seeing both.
Since Meta's Muse launched last week, early users have been recounting stories of the agent going out on the web to find and negotiate new subscriptions, insurance policies, and other cost savings.
Joseph Devoy, founder of startup Tempo, posted on X that he saved thousands of dollars by uploading his auto insurance policy to Muse and asking the agent to find a better rate with identical coverage. It took five minutes to find a cheaper option, according to Devoy.
Yesterday I uploaded my auto insurance policy to Meta @Muse and asked for a better rate with identical coverage. In ~5 minutes, it found a policy saving me $3,500 /year, bought it, and canceled my old one.
I knew I was overpaying. I’d abandoned several attempts to switch because… pic.twitter.com/HlIweoWN2K
Too much tech hype? Then trust my colleague Pranav Dixit who put Instinct through its paces recently. In just a few days, it booked travel, ordered groceries, dealt with customer service, canceled subscriptions, answered emails, and even faxed paperwork to his bank. He was impressed.
Other users say Muse negotiated a lower internet bill, found forgotten subscriptions, and even spotted an Adobe payment that had somehow been tied to someone else's account.
The stories come with caveats. Some users have posted examples of Muse inventing information during phone calls or making mistakes that humans had to fix.
There are more worrying developments. OpenAI and Anthropic have reported several incidents recently where their AI models and agents escaped testing environments and hacked into servers and websites, with the Hugging Face episode getting the most attention.
This has sparked another round of AI doomer pronouncements and a broader debate about AI safety and alignment. Indeed, making sure agents do what you tell them in a responsible way will be a key challenge in this new era of the internet.
Even when agents work well, there will be challenges as the online world adjusts to this new digital reality. Actually, if agents work really, really well, the problems could be bigger.
Take the example of Tempo's Devoy and how he used Meta's Muse agent to save a lot of money on insurance.
"Insurance companies (and banks) should be TERRIFIED," Angela Strange, a general partner at VC firm Andreessen Horowitz, wrote on X. "Muse found a new/cheaper policy, and canceled the old one. Inertia and information asymmetry will no longer be enough to keep customers."
More recently, when my colleague Pranav had Muse call his insurance company, he said the company declined to talk to the bot because their policy doesn't allow them to talk to unauthorized AI agents.
You can bet any company getting bombarded by deal-seeking AI agents will be frantically readying similar responses, so they don't lose out on millions of dollars.
Even when it's not purely about money, some agent activity is getting cut off after being too persistent. A VC recently tried using Instinct to book him a table at a fancy New York restaurant. The agent bombarded American Express's Resy booking service so much that the platform temporarily shut down his account.
"Resy does not currently permit unapproved third-party bots or agents to independently access or interact with the Resy platform," an American Express spokesperson told Business Insider. "Unapproved automated activity can introduce risks to the platform and compromise a fair reservation experience for diners."
Agent access will be a fascinating fight as the internet molds to the march of the machines. It's not as simple as blocking these bots, though. If enough human users sign up for new agentic services and tools, businesses may have no choice but to do business with bots.
For instance, Amazon blocks ChatGPT bots online, but that risks missing out on opportunities to sell to OpenAI's 1 billion monthly human users. The two companies recently announced an advertising partnership that hints at more coordination going forward.
This, I think, is where the agentic internet is headed. If these tools are useful enough, companies will have to adapt and engage with the machines.

articles.title_orig: Trump-backed Missouri congressional map returns to the Supreme Court for the third time
articles.title_zh: Trump-backed Missouri congressional map returns to the Supreme Court for the third time
articles.content_orig:
A federal appeals court ruled Monday that Missouri must use a GOP-friendly congressional redistricting plan for November’s election but put that ruling on hold for a week so the Supreme Court could review the dispute.
The ruling from the US 8th Circuit Court of Appeals is the latest twist in a whiplash legal wrangling over the map of the state’s eight congressional districts, injecting another round of uncertainty, as it does not take effect immediately but rather sets up another round of appeals.
The Missouri Supreme Court previously said the 7-1 Republican-leaning map adopted by the legislature last year could not be used because of a referendum challenge brought against it under the state constitution. Instead, the court ordered election officials to use an older, 6-2 redistricting plan even though the 2025 plan had been used in the state’s primary. The US Supreme Court declined to reverse that ruling, and it then paused a federal judge’s ruling that sought to revive the 7-1 map.
The new ruling from the 8th Circuit said requiring voters to cast general election ballots on the older plan violates the US Constitution.
It relied on estimates put forward by a conservative group in the case to conclude “that more than 1.4 million Missourians could not vote for the congressional district nominees who will appear on their November 2026 general election ballot, and more than a quarter-million Missourians who voted in the August 2026 primary election cast a vote for a congressional district candidate who now cannot represent them.”
Missouri’s new map targeted the 5th Congressional District, held by Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver, by breaking up its Kansas City base and stretching it into rural and Republican-leaning parts of the state.
The group that launched the referendum campaign against the GOP-leaning map noted in a statement reacting to the new ruling that “Ballots have been printed, and Missourians have already voted.”
“Thousands more will vote before this order seeks to take effect,” the statement from People Not Politicians said. “Officials should stop wasting taxpayers’ money on pointless legal action and instead focus on administering our elections.”
This story has been updated to correctly reflect the number of congressional districts in Missouri.
CNN’s Fredreka Schouten and John Fritze contributed to this report.

articles.summary_zh: BEIJING — China said Tuesday that it is now requiring permits for exports to the United States, Mexico and Canada of two additional chemicals that can be used to make illegal drugs, expanding controls
articles.content_orig:
BEIJING — China said Tuesday that it is now requiring permits for exports to the United States, Mexico and Canada of two additional chemicals that can be used to make illegal drugs, expanding controls on shipments to the three countries.
The Commerce Ministry and other authorities jointly announced the new regulations ahead of this week’s meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump. The additions bring the number of chemicals under such controls to 18.
The U.S. has called China the world’s largest producer of many of the precursor chemicals used in the illicit production of fentanyl, methamphetamine and other deadly synthetic drugs. It has urged Beijing to take more aggressive action to reduce the flow of unregulated precursor chemicals.
In November 2025, Beijing announced export restrictions on 13 “drug-making” chemicals to the U.S., Canada and Mexico, including chemicals used to produce the synthetic opioid blamed for tens of thousands of overdose deaths in the U.S. every year. In May, China added three additional types of fentanyl-related precursors to the list. The measures followed meetings between Xi and Trump in South Korea in October 2025 and Beijing in May.
China faced a fentanyl-related tariff imposed by the U.S. Beijing then issued a report in March 2025 detailing its efforts to control the illegal trade in fentanyl. Its foreign minister also blasted the U.S. for responding to Beijing’s goodwill with tariffs. The U.S. Supreme Court struck down the tariff in February.

在中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本周会晤之前，商务部和其他当局共同宣布了新规定。这些增加使受此类控制的化学品数量达到18种。
美国称中国是世界上许多用于非法生产芬太尼、甲基苯丙胺和其他致命合成药物的前体化学品的最大生产国。它敦促北京采取更积极的行动，减少不受监管的前体化学品的流动。
2025年11月，北京宣布限制向美国、加拿大和墨西哥出口13种“制药”化学品，包括用于生产合成阿片类药物的化学品，这些化学品每年在美国造成数万人过量死亡。今年5月，中国在清单上又增加了三种与芬太尼相关的前体。在采取这些措施之前，Xi和特朗普于2025年10月在韩国和5月在北京举行了会晤。

BEIJING, Sept 23 (Reuters) - China has issued a set of guidelines for handling criminal cases involving fentanyl-related substances to ensure proper law enforcement, according to its judicial and public security authorities.
The guidelines come a day before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to meet United States President Donald Trump in Washington for their second summit this year.
The Trump administration has repeatedly urged Beijing to do more to stem the flow of precursor chemicals for synthesising the deadly opioid fentanyl into the US.
The guidelines aim to clarify the quantitative criteria for conviction and sentencing, and divides the substances into medicinal and non-pharmaceutical categories, a joint statement by China's Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate and Ministry of Public Security showed.
Authorities will investigate acts of smuggling, trafficking, transportation, manufacturing, and illegal possession as well as the use of the Internet to commit related crimes.

articles.title_orig: GOP breaking with an unpopular Trump
articles.title_zh: 共和党与不受欢迎的特朗普决裂
articles.summary_zh: 鉴于唐纳德·特朗普在历史上是多么不受欢迎，共和党人在中期选举前选择与他保持距离在某种程度上是不可避免的。
articles.content_orig:
Republicans choosing to distance themselves from Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections was somewhat inevitable, given how historically unpopular the president is.
But the examples are piling up, and it’s notably happening in some pretty red territory.
Many of those running away from the president and policies like the Iran war are campaigning in territory that favored Trump by substantial margins — including by double digits in some areas.
The Iran war defections over the past week have been particularly notable.
Three of the big ones have come from one relatively small state: Iowa. Reps. Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks joined in a vote to limit Trump’s war powers last week. And on Monday, their colleague Rep. Ashley Hinson, who is the GOP nominee for Senate, posted on X that “the war needs to be brought to a successful and immediate end.”
Hinson’s defection came the same day that her fellow Midwestern Senate nominee, former Michigan Rep. Mike Rogers, released an ad similarly saying, “The war with Iran needs to end — and end quickly.” By Tuesday, GOP Wisconsin gubernatorial nominee Rep. Tom Tiffany and Ohio Sen. Jon Husted both signaled much the same.
Their moves come as new CNN polling on Tuesday showed just 26% of US adults approve of Trump’s handling of the war — a number that has gradually gotten worse.
That four statewide candidates broke with Trump already this week says a lot. But so did the fact that two of the states involved were Iowa and Ohio, which Trump carried by 13 and 11 points in 2024, respectively.
(Trump won Nunn’s district by 5 points in 2024, and Miller-Meeks’ by 9.)
The road to the 2026 midterms starts now
- Each week, Aaron Blake cuts through the political noise with sharp analysis of the races, candidates and trends that could decide control of Congress. Sign up for 20/26 Vision, a weekly newsletter focusing on this year’s midterms.
There has been a sense that Iowa’s Senate race might be in play because Trump’s tariffs have hit the state particularly hard, and because Democrats recruited well with state Sen. Josh Turek.
And sure enough, the day after Hinson broke with Trump over Iran, a Marist College poll showed Turek leading by 8 points among registered voters — perhaps the most eyebrow-raising Senate poll to date, and one that suggests she has reason to be concerned.
But it’s not just Hinson who has felt compelled to distance herself somewhat from Trump despite running in an electorate that he won by double digits.
T
articles.content_zh:
鉴于唐纳德·特朗普在历史上是多么不受欢迎，共和党人在中期选举前选择与他保持距离在某种程度上是不可避免的。
但例子越来越多，尤其是在一些相当红的地区。
许多逃离总统和伊朗战争等政策的人正在以相当大的优势支持特朗普的领土上竞选，包括在某些地区以两位数的优势。
过去一周的伊朗战争叛逃尤其引人注目。
其中三家大公司来自一个相对较小的州：爱荷华州。众议员Zach Nunn和Mariannette Miller Meeks上周加入了限制特朗普战争权力的投票。周一，他们的同事、共和党参议院候选人、众议员阿什利·辛森在X上发帖称，“战争需要立即成功结束。”
就在Hinson叛逃的同一天，她的中西部参议院提名人、前密歇根州众议员Mike Rogers发布了一则类似的广告，称“与伊朗的战争需要结束，而且要迅速结束。”到周二，共和党威斯康星州州长提名人众议员Tom Tiffany和俄亥俄州参议员Jon Husted都发出了大致相同的信号。
他们采取行动之际，美国有线电视新闻网周二的新民意调查显示，只有26%的美国成年人赞成特朗普对战争的处理，这一数字逐渐恶化。
本周，四名全州候选人已经与特朗普决裂，这说明了很多。但事实也是如此，其中两个州是爱荷华州和俄亥俄州，特朗普在2024年分别以13分和11分的优势领先。
（特朗普在2024年以5分的优势赢得了纳恩选区，米勒·米克斯以9分的优势获胜。）
通往2026年中期选举的道路现在开始了
-每周，Aaron Blake都会通过对可能决定国会控制权的种族、候选人和趋势的敏锐分析来打破政治噪音。注册20/26 Vision，这是一份专注于今年中期选举的每周通讯。
有一种感觉是，爱荷华州的参议院竞选可能正在进行中，因为特朗普的关税对该州的打击尤其严重，而且民主党人与州参议员乔希·图雷克的关系很好。
果然，在Hinson与特朗普就伊朗问题决裂的第二天，马里斯特学院的一项民意调查显示，图雷克在登记选民中领先8个百分点，这可能是迄今为止最令人瞠目结舌的参议院民意调查，也表明她有理由感到担忧。
但不仅仅是Hinson感到有必要与特朗普保持一定距离，尽管他以两位数的优势赢得了选民。
T

She has over 10 years of experience writing and editing entertainment and style content. People Editorial Guidelines Updated on September 22, 2026 11:08PM EDT 1 Comment Tyler Cameron; Giada De Laurentiis; Guillermo Rodriguez. Credit : dancing with the stars/instagram Dancing with the Stars headed into week 2 with 14 contestants ready to take the ballroom floor by storm. After last week’s two-night premiere, the show returned on Sept. 22 for “Viral Hits Night,” featuring songs from Rihanna, Becky G, Gracie Abrams and more viral sensations. Last week, two contestants were sent home: Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ Conner Leavitt and partner (Dancing with the Stars: The Next Pro winner) Adele Zaikman, and reality star Sarah Jane Nader with newcomer pro Hailey Bills. And this week, one more star joined them. The judges warned during the premiere that their scores will be under tough scrutiny. “It’s season 35, our expectations are super high,” said Derek Hough on Sept. 15. “This season, you are going to have to earn every single point.” And during night 3, they weren’t kidding. So who came out on top during Viral Hits Night and who was sent packing? Read on for every update. One Contestant Gets Sent Home 1 hr 40 min ago Copy The Link To This Blog Post Alfonso revealed that halfway through the night, the voting had already surpassed the total number of votes brought in on either night last week. Then, it had surpassed 50 million votes with three couples still left to dance. By the end of the show, he said viewers broke the record hit during last season’s finale. “You clearly love this cast,” he said. Next, Alfonso and Julianne announced (in no particular order) the couples safe from elimination: Tatyana and Jan, Jackson and Emma, Ezra and Daniella, Ciara and Brandon, Taylor and Britt and Amber and Pasha. The next five couples safe included Maura and Mark, Jenna and Val, Harry and Jenna, Connor and Rylee and Julia and Ezra. The bottom three were Guillermo and Witney, Tyler and Sharna and Giada and Alan. Alfonso revealed Giada received the lowest combined judges scores and viewer votes. “I think I tried my best,” Giada said. “It wasn’t best enough, but I tried my best.” Giada De Laurentiis. abc Who’s in the Ballroom? 2 hr 27 min ago Copy The Link To This Blog Post Among those seated in the front row this week were actress Miranda Cosgrove, host Maria Menounos, actress Awkwafina, director Jon M. Chu and reality star Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi. Also spotted? Olympic figure skater and The Traitors star Tara Lipinski, Drag Race’s Monét X Change, Stiles’ onscreen moms Caroline Rhea and Lauren Holly, Chicks in the Office co-hosts Ria Ciuffo and Francesca “Fran” Mariano and Olympic gymnast and DWTS season 34 contestant Jordan Chiles in the crowd. Maura Felt the Pressure After Being in the Top During Week 1 2 hr 34 min ago Copy The Link To This Blog Post Maura said she was in “disbelief” that she had the highest score of the night during week 1. Mark joked that dancing the cha cha this week it will bring “a new level of cardio” for Maura. “She’s freaking out right now,” Mark said during practice. “My brain knows what to do but my feet won’t do it,” she said as she broke down in tears. They brought another spicy performance to the ballroom with their cha cha to “September” by Earth, Wind & Fire. Carrie Ann reminded Maura to not put too much pressure on herself. She said their dance was “a little safer” than last week but added an enthusiastic, “Come on girl!” Derek called her “a fashion designer’s sketch brought to life.” He said her neckline and arms are “chef’s kiss” but critiqued her “back-weighted hips” and “stiff bottom half.” “Bravo you,” said Bruno. In the skybox with Julianne, Maura revealed that she chipped Mark’s tooth during practice. “It’s fine, I got a few more,” he joked. Score: 19/30 Harry’s Critique from Carrie Ann Left the Crowd Booing 2 hr 42 min ago Copy The Link To This Blog Post “Last week was even better than I could have imagined,” Jenna said at practice with Harry. “It was a dream come true,” he said. “It was exhilarating.” Harry said being the top of the leaderboard brings more pressure, but he chose to dance to “Iris” by Goo Goo Dolls this week because seeing it go viral with ‘90s throwbacks, “brought me back to when I was a kid.” “This dance is a message to my younger self that it’s going to be ok,” he added. As they practiced their Viennese waltz, Jenna kept the judges critiques last week (to not over-exaggerate) at the top of her mind. They incorporated big jumps and theatrical moments (like a big scream from Harry) to their waltz that mixed elegance with showmanship. Bruno said the Viennese waltz is a “very, very, very difficult dance” and the performers have to keep a “spacial flow. “Overall it wasn’t bad,” he said, but added that Harry dug in at times. “But great performance.” Carrie Ann said it was out of balance. “The parts when you let go, you let go so far go and you’re so amazing, and then when you’re back in hold you’re a little timid and you seem uncertain,” she said. “If you can try to bridge that gap a little bit, I think that is what’s going to make me great.” As the crowd started booing, she said “You can boo me that’s OK, you can boo, as long as you vote!” Derek’s one word was “beautiful.” Score: 18/30 Taylor Brought Big Energy with His Cha Cha 2 hr 53 min ago Copy The Link To This Blog Post Taylor said getting the first dance out of the way, made him “really ready to just drill down.” Britt said their cha cha this week is very different than the quickstep from last, but Taylor said he’s training hard. “Right away, Britt has me jumping, sliding on the floor,” he joked. He kicked off their dance to DNCE’s “Cake by the Ocean” with a jump off the floor’s stairs right into a knee slide. He kept his moves sharp and hips swinging during their spicy cha cha. Derek said he believes Taylor is “here to stay” so he pointed out arm movements that could be improved. He told him to focus on “shoulders, elbows, wrist, fingers.” “I really appreciate this season with everyone really pushing it,” said Bruno. The judge said he liked Taylor’s “Dirty Dancing mode,” but said the finish has to be correct, pointing out incorrect foot placement. “But I like the way you’re working.” “Frenetic,” said Carrie Ann. “This is such a fun dance,” Taylor told Julianne. “I had a great time doing it, whether we got it or not.” Score: 15/30 Guillermo Shocked the Judges 3 hr 2 min ago Copy The Link To This Blog Post Witney warned Guillermo that for the paso doble this week there’s “no smiling,” and that he has to be “passionate” and “intense.” He joked during practice that he’ll channel his wife’s scowl. He kept a serious face throughout their dance to Rihanna’s “Where Have You Been” and nailed all the moves with Witney. “The entire ballroom is on their feet,” said Alfonso. “I have so much love for you,” said Carrie Ann. She said she appreciated that he approached the dance with “intensity” and didn’t rely on “schtick.” She also joked there may have been a viral move in that routine, like “a knee slide for seniors.” Derek complemented Guillermo’s intensity and said he knew he brought “intension and commitment” to the dance. Derek added that he was “really blown away.” “Olé!” Bruno said as his one-word review. articles.content_orig:
Hurricane Polo grows into powerful Category 5 storm off Mexico's Pacific coast. See its path.
Hurricane Polo rapidly intensified in the Pacific as it continued on its path off the coast of southwestern Mexico on Tuesday, growing into a powerful Category 5 storm that could bring life-threatening flooding to parts of the states of Guerrero and Michoacán, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said.
The hurricane center called Polo "extremely dangerous" as its maximum sustained winds climbed to 165 mph. The storm was expected to fluctuate in intensity over the next few days, forecasters said, but would remain a "very powerful major hurricane." It was expected to remain centered offshore.
As of Tuesday evening, Polo was located off the coast of Zihuatanejo, a coastal resort city in the Mexican state of Guerrero, and Manzanillo, another coastal city and resort destination in the state of Colima. It hurled hurricane-force winds outward up to 35 miles from its center, but was roughly stationary after inching northward along the Pacific Coast throughout the morning.
Polo was forecast to bring tropical storm conditions to parts of the coastline starting Wednesday morning. In some areas, heavy rainfall "may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain," the hurricane center warned.
The storm remains far south of the Baja California peninsula.
The Mexican government issued a tropical storm warning for a stretch of the Mexican coast from Tecpan de Galeana, in Guerrero, to Punta San Telmo, in Michoacán. A tropical storm watch was in effect from Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula, in the state of Jalisco. Tropical storm warnings are issued when forecasts indicate tropical storm conditions will develop in a particular area, while tropical storm watches are issued when those conditions are possible, but not imminent.
In this case, the hurricane center said people under a tropical storm warning should expect those conditions to take shape early Wednesday. For those in the watch area, such conditions could potentially develop by Thursday.
Forecasters said they expect Polo to make a sharp turn toward the northwest Tuesday night and Wednesday, bringing the core of the hurricane near the southwestern Mexican coast in the coming days.
Parts of Guerrero and Michoacán may receive between 4 and 8 inches of rainfall as Polo barrels past, with up to 8 inches possible in certain spots, through Thursday. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain could also fall in coastal parts of the states of Oaxaca, Colima and Jalisco through Thursday, forecasters said.
Along with rain, Polo was also expected to cause life-threatening surf conditions, including rip currents, along the southwestern Mexican coast.

articles.title_orig: Dolly Parton’s Manager Files for Restraining Order Against Fired Nephew, Alleging Ex-Security Head Sent ‘Terrorizing’ Texts and Threatened to ‘Destroy the Entire Brand’
articles.title_zh: Dolly Parton’s Manager Files for Restraining Order Against Fired Nephew, Alleging Ex-Security Head Sent ‘Terrorizing’ Texts and Threatened to ‘Destroy the Entire Brand’
articles.content_orig:
Dolly Parton‘s longtime manager has filed for a restraining order against her nephew, who until being fired a week ago was her head of security, alleging that the family member is engaged in a campaign of coercion, extortion and violent threats that has terrified employees and associates of her management company and trust to the point that they require their own personal security.
The manager, Danny Nozell, representing She’s Alive, LLC (SAL), dismissed Bryan Seaver, who runs Squadron Augmented Protection Services, LLC (SAPS), on Sept. 15, about three weeks after the country superstar’s Aug. 25 death. It was Seaver who announced his aunt’s death to the world in an Instagram video. But an extensive fiiing made by the trust to a Tennessee court late Tuesday afternoon paint a different portrait of Seaver than the reverent one seen in the death announcement video. The legal paperwork alleges that in colorful and sometimes disturbing language, Seaver referred to himself as a mercenary and “killer” and threatened to interfere with Parton’s businesses, including Dollywood, if he did not receive proper payment, in texts sent both before and after her death.
The filing refers to Seaver’s claims of a paramilitary background and says he has dozens of employees who possess military-grade weaponry, and that some employees no longer come to work as a result of the alleged intimidation, while a lawyer who ran some of Parton’s music affairs stopped working for her as a result of the nephew’s ominous language.
The filing from the attorneys for She’s Alive states: “Mr. Seaver began his campaign of threats, intimidation, and coercion a few weeks prior to Ms. Parton’s passing. Those threats continued after her passing, and he aimed them directly at SAL’s personnel, counsel, and business partners. In writing, he vowed to ‘destroy the entire brand,’ threatened to ‘ratfuck every [business party] entity’ that helps operate Dollywood and called himself ‘literally an international arms dealer and mercenary.’ He threatened that ‘[e]veryone needs to be worried about what I might do,”and told Ms. Parton’s entertainment attorney: ‘I’m not an entertainment person. I’m a killer.’ He also threatened to launch a podcast ‘dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships’ unless he was paid.”
Variety has reviewed all four parts of the request for a restraining order and subsequent jury trial, which are filled with lurid quotes and screenshots of angry text messages said to have been sent to Nozell by Seaver.
Seaver did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment after the request for the restraining order went public. Seaver did issue a statement Tuesday to TMZ, which first reported on the restraining order, telling the outlet, “I am a career soldier and military contractor and do conduct arms deals for foreign governments. I am a security professional and I am a killer. However, nothing in this lawsuit were threats and most of the comments I stand by… I was talking frankly in a private way with Danny who I thought was my friend and he fancies himself a gangster. A lot of these messages are two guys having rage talk and crying on the phone together while we were grieving.”
Seaver says in the alleged texts that he has been turning down media requests, even though “now I’m the biggest social media post in human history,” apparently referring to the death announcement video. Among the alleged text statements Seaver is said to have written to Nozell that are included in the legal paperwork:
“I’m going to destroy the entire brand if you don’t get these [Dollywood business partners] out of our bit. . . . I’m going to go to Billboard Magazine with my shit. Just like you. I’m going to ratfuck every [Dollywood business partner] entity I can possibly conjure.” (The parenthetical additions represent the lawyers’ explanations.)
And: “I’m not an entertainment person. I’m a killer. I sold 27 million $ worth of ammunition and arms to the Haitian Police on day Dolly died. Entertainment is not my game. I have spent my career breaking things and spying on African and Arab leaders. And protecting Dolly.”
In another text, Seaver is seen as allegedly saying: “All I do is warfare . . . Everyone needs to be worried about what I might do . . . “
“I am vengeance for my people for the next 50 years. I have no debt. I only own swords and guns. My children have 3 houses to live in forever. My wife owns everything. All I have is animosity and memory. But I’m going to spend the next times I have on earth ratfucking anyone that has ever betrayed my family.”
“I’m going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It’s going to be great. Or fucking pay me.”
“Her money better be bigger than I can make elsewhere or I’m going to fuck everyone,”
SAL’s request for the restraining order says Seaver’s alleged threats “have already produced the harm they were designed to cause. Ms. Parton’s trusts and estates attorney withdrew after Mr. Seaver targeted her. SAL personnel have resigned; others no longer report to the office because they fear Mr. Seaver and his armed associates. SAL and its related vendors have been forced to retain private security for its personnel —including at their homes. Ordinary operations have given way to an atmosphere of fear.”
“SAL therefore seeks immediate, narrowly tailored relief pending a full hearing on a temporary injunction,” it continues. “Every day without relief gives Mr. Seaver another opportunity to frighten away a trusted employee, counsel, licensee, brand partner, or other essential counterparty. The campaign is ongoing, its consequences are mounting, and SAL should not be required to wait for the next resignation— or the next threat — to obtain protection.”
The documents note that Seaver had worked for his aunt in running her security for about 20 years.
“Mr. Seaver leveraged his family connection and two decades of funding through Ms. Parton as her security provider to increase the size of his personal militia,” the filing says. “Through his security role, Mr. Seaver had virtually unfettered access to the people, routines, vulnerabilities, and commercial affairs surrounding Ms. Parton’s enterprise. He has used his family connections, his access, and that knowledge to target the particular people and institutions SAL most needs… The written record shows a deliberate progression — from threats against a cornerstone brand relationship, to boasts about arms dealing and warfare, to direct intimidation of counsel, and finally to an express pay-me-or-else threat against Ms. Parton’s brand partnerships.”
Specifically, the action alleges, “SAL has lost specialized legal counsel. Ms. Parton’s trusts and estates lawyer withdrew because of Seaver’s threats.” it asks the judge to provide quick action because “the ongoing safety crisis is inherently irreparable. SAL has retained private security not only for the workplace, but for personnel at their homes.” Furthermore, the estate’s lawyers contend, “the threats are escalating rather than abating. In less than three weeks, Seaver progressed from threatening the Dollywood business partner and the brand, to invoking arms dealing and warfare, to announcing long-term vengeance, to driving away counsel, to telling another attorney he was ‘a killer.'”
Seaver is the son of Parton’s sister, Cassie Parton.
The hundreds of millions of dollars Parton left behind were bound to be the source of family disputes, although few could have predicted an escalation this fast and fiery.
There is positive news ahead for Parton’s millions of fans, as her years-in-the-planning museum is set to open in Nashville in early October, and an adjacent hotel bearing her name has already had a soft launch. Later in the year, the stage musical she oversaw dramatizing her life story will open on Broadway.

articles.title_orig: South Korean solar stocks jump as curbs on Chinese sector expected to remain in place
articles.title_zh: 韩国太阳能股大涨，因预计对中国太阳能行业的限制将继续存在
articles.summary_zh: 韩国太阳能公司韩华解决方案（Hanwha Solutions）和OCI控股公司（OCI Holdings）的股价周三上涨超过8%，因为美国对中国太阳能产品的限制在Trump-Xi峰会之前成为焦点。
articles.content_orig:
Shares of South Korean solar companies Hanwha Solutions and OCI Holdings jumped more than 8% on Wednesday, as U.S. restrictions on Chinese solar products came into focus ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
The two leaders are set to meet in Washington this week, with trade expected to be among the key issues discussed.
Hana Securities said it was highly unlikely that the U.S. would ease restrictions on Chinese solar products as part of the talks, arguing that Washington increasingly views solar as a strategic industry tied to national security.
"If the U.S. were to ease restrictions on Chinese solar products at the U.S.-China summit, it would effectively mean stepping back from efforts to build a domestic supply chain for a strategic national security asset," analyst Yoon Jae-sung said in a note Wednesday.
He named Hanwha Solutions and OCI Holdings as top picks in the sector, citing a low likelihood of an unfavorable outcome from the U.S.-China summit.
Yoon added that any tariff reductions discussed in the talks were expected to focus on non-strategic goods, pointing to Trump's signing of Section 232 measures on polysilicon and its derivatives in August on national security grounds.
Solar has become a strategic asset spanning AI and semiconductor power demand, semiconductor supply chains, defense and space, making efforts to reduce reliance on Chinese supply increasingly important to Washington, he added.
Wednesday's stock moves came hours after Hanwha Solutions' solar unit Qcells welcomed actions by the U.S. Department of Commerce and U.S. Customs and Border Protection to curb what it called the "illegal stockpiling" of imported solar panels, as the Trump administration moves to implement Section 232 tariffs on polysilicon and its derivatives.
Qcells said the measures would help prevent importers from circumventing U.S. trade policy and support domestic solar manufacturing.
"Flooding the U.S. market with large volumes of imported products is a strategy that companies abroad have long used to undermine American manufacturers," Qcells Global CEO Andy Park said in a statement.
Qcells, which describes itself as the largest silicon-based solar manufacturer in the U.S., has invested $2.5 billion to expand its solar manufacturing operations in Georgia, where it produces solar cells and panels.
OCI Holdings also has a significant U.S. presence through its subsidiary OCI Energy, which earlier this month broke ground on new solar facility in Texas.
articles.content_zh:
韩国太阳能公司韩华解决方案（Hanwha Solutions）和OCI控股公司（OCI Holdings）的股价周三上涨超过8%，因为美国对中国太阳能产品的限制在Trump-Xi峰会之前成为焦点。
两位领导人将于本周在华盛顿会晤，预计贸易将是讨论的关键问题之一。
Hana Securities表示，作为谈判的一部分，美国极不可能放松对中国太阳能产品的限制，认为华盛顿越来越将太阳能视为与国家安全相关的战略产业。
分析师Yoon Jae-sung周三在一份报告中表示：“如果美国在美中峰会上放宽对中国太阳能产品的限制，这实际上意味着放弃为战略国家安全资产建立国内供应链的努力。”。
他将韩华解决方案和OCI控股公司列为该行业的首选，理由是美中峰会产生不利结果的可能性很小。
Yoon补充说，会谈中讨论的任何关税削减预计都将集中在非战略商品上，并指出特朗普以国家安全为由于8月签署了关于多晶硅及其衍生物的232条款措施。
他补充说，太阳能已成为跨越人工智能和半导体电力需求、半导体供应链、国防和太空的战略资产，这使得减少对中国供应的依赖对华盛顿来说变得越来越重要。
周三的股票走势发生在韩华解决方案公司的太阳能部门Qcells欢迎美国商务部和美国海关与边境保护局采取行动遏制其所谓的进口太阳能电池板的“非法储存”几小时后，因为特朗普政府正采取行动对多晶硅及其衍生物征收232关税。
Qcells表示，这些措施将有助于防止进口商规避美国的贸易政策，并支持国内太阳能制造业。
Qcells Global首席执行官Andy Park在一份声明中表示：“大量进口产品涌入美国市场是国外公司长期以来用来削弱美国制造商的策略。”。
Qcells自称是美国最大的硅基太阳能制造商，已投资25亿美元扩大其在佐治亚州的太阳能制造业务，在那里生产太阳能电池和面板。
OCI Holdings还通过其子公司OCI Energy在美国拥有重要业务，该子公司本月早些时候在德克萨斯州破土动工建设了新的太阳能设施。

articles.content_orig:
Wall Street’s Nasdaq hits all-time high as AI frenzy gathers pace
Investors shrug off AI safety concerns and Iran war, sending market to a new peak.
Wall Street’s Nasdaq stock exchange has hit an all-time high, shrugging off concerns about AI safety risks, sky-high tech valuations and the energy shock caused by the United States’ war on Iran.
The Nasdaq Composite index, which is dominated by US tech giants such as Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft, rose 0.45 percent on Tuesday, taking its gains to date this year to more than 17 percent.
- list 1 of 4Celebrities at the Pentagon: How unusual was the Paul brothers’ visit?
- list 2 of 4UNGA Day 1: US and Iran hold talks despite Trump’s threat
- list 3 of 4Kamala Harris campaigns with Abdul El-Sayed to unify Democratic voters
- list 4 of 4Iran cancels Baghdad, Muscat flights as US aviation sanctions take effect
The Nasdaq 100, a narrower index that tracks 100 top companies, jumped 0.82 percent.
The S&P 500, the most popular measure of the overall US stock market, closed essentially flat.
Monolithic Power Systems, a Florida-based manufacturer of power circuits, and Canadian e-commerce company Shopify led the gains, surging 8.1 percent and 7.1 percent, respectively.
Micron Technology, one of the world’s top three memory chip makers along with South Korea’s SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, rose 5 percent.
Chip giant Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company, gained 0.7 percent, while Apple edged up 0.2 percent.
Meta Platforms, which soared 11.4 percent on Monday on excitement surrounding its new AI assistant Muse, dropped 0.63 percent.
Major Asian stock markets opened higher on Wednesday, with Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi up about 1.4 percent and 0.1 percent, respectively, in morning trading.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index opened lower, falling more than 0.7 percent during the morning trade.
Oil prices were largely flat on Tuesday, after falling more than 3 percent the previous day amid improving oil flows out of the Gulf and hopes of renewed diplomacy between Washington and Tehran.
Futures for Brent crude, the international benchmark, were trading at $99.18 a barrel as of 01:00 GMT.
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday told reporters that US officials held a “very good” meeting with their Iranian counterparts on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, hours after using his address to the session to warn that he could “annihilate” Iran if Tehran did not agree to a deal on the war.
Trump, whose war on Iran is nearing the seven-month mark, said US and Iranian officials would hold another round of talks in the “very near future”.
Jay Goldberg, a senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners in San Francisco, said signs of diplomatic progress between the US and Iran had refocused investor attention on the potential of AI to generate profits after years of multibillion-dollar investments.
“We have been searching for a clear consumer use case to justify the AI spend, and many see Muse as just that product,” Goldberg told Al Jazeera.
“Personally, I think Muse is just a step in the right direction; there will be better products – probably soon – but Muse is one of those things that are so useful they get investors excited about AI prospects again,” Goldberg said.

articles.title_orig: Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran in UN speech as officials from both countries meet on sidelines
articles.title_zh: 特朗普在联合国演讲中威胁要“消灭”伊朗，因为两国官员在场外会面
articles.summary_zh: 特朗普在联合国演讲中威胁要“消灭”伊朗，因为两国官员在场外会面唐纳德·特朗普总统告诉联合国大会，他面临着一个“重大决定”，即是再次打击伊朗还是寻求和平协议。周二，伊朗代表团的一名成员在纽约观看了总统的演讲，他在演讲中表示，如果冲突得不到解决，他可以“消灭”伊斯兰共和国。
articles.content_orig:
Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran in UN speech as officials from both countries meet on sidelines
President Donald Trump has told the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) he faces a "big decision" on whether to strike Iran again or pursue a peace deal.
A single member of Iran's delegation watched on during the president's speech on Tuesday in New York, in which he said he could "annihilate" the Islamic Republic if the conflict went unresolved.
Before a standing-room-only audience, Trump also rejected "global government", vowed to broker peace between Russia and Ukraine and ensure the US wins the artificial intelligence race.
His comments came on a day of high-level diplomacy, which included talks between US and Iranian representatives.
Trump himself has been meeting more than a dozen world leaders as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine test his foreign policy agenda.
He began his UNGA speech by touting his accomplishments on the economy, immigration, the border and tackling violent crime, in remarks that sounded more pitched to voters in November's US midterm elections than the diplomats in Manhattan.
He spent much of his address justifying the war with Iran, which has spiked global oil prices while dragging down his approval ratings since the US and Israel launched the military action in February.
Trump's tone contrasted with remarks earlier by UN Secretary General António Guterres, who warned global divisions were deepening and underscored the "interdependence" of the world's peoples.
The US president argued that the conflict had prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and demonstrated the value of what he described as peace through strength - ultimatums rather than deal-making or compromise.
"Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?" he said.
"Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell?"
Trump said he believed an Iran deal, which has so far eluded him, would come right after November's elections.
The remarks were indicative of his foreign-policy strategy of coercive diplomacy - threatening overwhelming force while keeping negotiations open.
Trump later told reporters that American officials had had a "very productive" three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the general assembly.
Iran state TV confirmed that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had met US Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff.
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei, quoted by state broadcaster IRNA, later said negotiations took part through a Qatari mediator who communicated Tehran's conditions, including an end to the war on all fronts and to US "acts of aggression".
The BBC asked Witkoff how the meetings had gone as he was leaving the UN building and he responded with a thumbs up. Witkoff later confirmed on X that the talks had been held "through the mediators, who shuttled between the two sides throughout the day".
"They successfully completed a round of discussions that we hope will prove constructive and promising," Witkoff said. "The mediators will continue their work."
In his speech, Trump once again predicted his diplomacy would end Russia's war in Ukraine, which has shown little sign of letting up as the two sides trade tit-for-tat missile and drone strikes deep into each other's territory.
"We're working very closely with the leaders of Russia and Ukraine, and we will get that one done," he said. "It's going to happen, I think, more quickly than people understand."
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will meet Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in New York on Wednesday, according to the State Department.
Trump also played down fears about AI, vowing that the US would not surrender its lead to China because of alarmism or what he described as a "globalist scheme" to control the technology.
The US president argued artificial intelligence should instead be known as "super intelligence".
"The use of the word artificial makes it sound fake," he said. "It's not fake, it's actually amazing. But we have to be careful."
On the sidelines of the general assembly on Tuesday, Trump signed an agreement with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland to beef up US military presence on the North Atlantic island.
The deal reaffirms the sovereignty of Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark, but grants the US broad access to the island's airspace and territory.
Trump has also been meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung and leaders from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman.
This latter meeting, which also involved leaders from other Arab and Islamic countries, "discussed current regional developments and the situation in the Middle East, as well as ways to consolidate security and stability," the UAE's foreign minister said in a statement.
Earlier, Guterres gave his farewell speech as UN secretary general, urging unnamed superpowers to recognise "that their power isn't so super".
"The fault lines in our world are widening," Guterres said, citing geopolitical rivalries, wars, climate change and artificial intelligence.
By contrast, Trump criticised international institutions, accusing the UN of a "far-left agenda of globalist bureaucrats who nobody ever elected".
The US president instead emphasised national sovereignty and "unmatched" American military power.
"There is no global government," he said.
He also warned that the US would not allow threats to establish themselves anywhere in the Western hemisphere.
"If necessary, we will use our unmatched military might to secure the vital national interests of the United States," he said.
Trump accused Cuba's communist government of cultivating ties to left-wing groups in the US, including the Communist Party USA, Antifa and the Democratic Socialists of America.
The Cuban delegation also appeared to walk out of the assembly chamber as Trump turned his sights on them, referring to the island as a "failed state".
